rules.name: branch-join
rules.derives: if/switch/try cost the channel-wise max of the test or discriminant and every branch, case, handler and finalizer, with an implicit empty else when the alternate is absent.
side_conditions: each branch goes through branch_reading_of (escape-lift) and sibling_of before the join
switch fall-through runs at most |cases| consecutive cases, a program constant
rules.evidence: [S1] The max over branches bounds any single path, and try/finally runs block+handler+finalizer at most once each, so a constant-count sum is covered. No uncertified side condition beyond §6.1/§6.4/§6.5. [S7 tests, compliant] Pinned by exact cost assertions on if/else joins and hot/cold selection; model fixture golden pins branches.ts.

rules.name: channel-total
rules.derives: A reading's total is the max over the Immediate/Normal part and every other non-Lazy channel (escapes and Scheduled). Lazy channels are excluded from total and read separately by latent().
side_conditions: lazy work is charged where it is consumed (for-of consumed_part_of, walker.rs:1369-1377; lazy-consume in summaries)
rules.evidence: [S1] Taking the max over the executed channels is sound because each channel is a path class. Excluding Lazy is sound only if every consumption site charges latent work; that pairing lives in E-family rules. Gap for §6.1/§6.4/§6.5 only. [S7 tests, compliant] Pinned by exact cost assertions at unit, integration and CLI level.

rules.name: expr-validity
rules.derives: Constructors for power, ratio, logarithm and factorial, with domain checks (positive, nonnegative, integer, valid) and constant evaluation. bind_inner rejects any result that is not valid.
side_conditions: positive() treats every Dimension as positive and Log(x) as positive whenever x is positive, which includes log(1) = 0 and log of a Ratio below 1
factorial requires an integer argument; x^0 = 1 only when x is positive
rules.evidence: [S1] The domain predicates encode the convention that dimensions are at least 1 and read Log as at least 1 (see also at_least_one, cost.rs:1068-1082). Log(Constant(1)) is accepted as positive though it equals 0. It arises from legacy LOG bound with no roots (bind pushes envelope 1, cost.rs:690-698) and from recurrence depth log(measure) when the measure is the constant 1 (recurrences.rs:294). No concrete bound violation was found, but the convention must be decided and encoded (gap S1-9 (G49)). [S7 tests, compliant] Rejection and diagnostic text asserted.

rules.name: limit-compare
rules.derives: Cost::compare returns Within when within(cost, limit), and Exceeds when within(limit, cost) and strictly_larger(cost, limit), else Inconclusive. The same within underlies max-dominance and charge_covers.
side_conditions: within: equality, 0, shared-envelope (poly, log) exponent order, per-dimension monomial order, log-of-product expansion, same-base exponential order, c^n and n! above monomials in n, a factor-wise product rule with factors at least 1, sum/max decomposition, power monotonicity, c^n <= n! and n! <= n^n
strictly_larger: envelope order, exponential/factorial dominance, max/product decomposition, monomial strict order, diagonal and single-dimension witness growth
proof-credit budget (COMPARISON_CREDITS); Inconclusive when exhausted
compares cost only; state ignored
rules.evidence: [S1] Each within/strictly_larger case checked holds for dimensions >= 1. The diagonal witness in strictly_larger is sound because a ∈ O(b) implies it along the diagonal. The one weak point is at_least_one(Log(_)) = true (cost.rs:1075), which licenses the product rule (cost.rs:1213-1217) through a factor log(1) = 0. That case is only reachable from the convention recorded in S1-9 (G49). Otherwise gap for §6.1/§6.4/§6.5. [S5 limit-compare-driver] S5-1 (G4), S5-2 (G31), S5-6 (G32). [S7 tests, compliant] Pinned: Within/Exceeds table in cost.test.rs (lines 100-102) plus lint exit and policy matrices. No test asserts an Exceeds verdict from a ceiling (4.2) or the 4.4 floor-based Exceeds wording.

rules.name: max-dominance
rules.derives: Part::max keeps one side when compare_legacy proves it dominates the other (Exceeds or Within), and builds Maximum(a, b) when the comparison is Inconclusive; unknowns, retained provenance and errors are joined.
side_conditions: equal preference rank on both sides (otherwise preference-rank decides)
compare_legacy binds legacy N to one fresh size dimension when neither side mentions a dimension (cost.rs:221-241)
rules.evidence: [S1] Dropping b when b is O(a) keeps a bound (max(a,b) is Theta(a)). Soundness rests on within/strictly_larger, reviewed under limit-compare. The trace keeps only the selected side on Within/Exceeds (cost.rs:1826-1849, traces.group only on Inconclusive), so the losing contribution is absent from the explanation (§6.5, gap S1-2 (G48)). [S7 tests, compliant] Unit tests pin canonical max terms; no integration test isolates dominance beyond the model golden (O(max(1, rows^2))).

rules.name: max-normalise
rules.derives: Maximum(...) flattens nested maxima, keeps the largest constant, dedups, and drops every term whose monomial is dominated per-dimension by another term's monomial (undominated_of).
side_conditions: monomial_within compares (power, log-power) pairs lexicographically per size dimension, over products, integer powers, ratios, dimensions and log(dimension)
constants never drop (dominance_of returns None)
skipped when more than MAX_REDUCED_TERMS terms
rules.evidence: [S1] Per-dimension lexicographic (p, q) order on n^p log^q n is a correct O-order for independent dimensions >= 1. Removing an O-dominated max term keeps the value within a constant factor. It relies on the dimensions-at-least-1 convention (gap S1-9 (G49)). [S7 tests, compliant] Exact canonical text/order asserted.

rules.name: nest-product
rules.derives: cost::nest multiplies a part by a factor, scaling its unknowns and retained provenance by the same factor. On multiply overflow or trace failure it keeps the unmultiplied inner cost and adds a ResourceExhaustion unknown.
side_conditions: factor is the proven multiplicity of the inner part
on overflow the printed cost is inner.cost with an unknown attached (cost.rs:2170-2178)
rules.evidence: [S1] The product rule is sound. The overflow fallback reports the body once in a Partial cost, the same floor defect as loop-unbounded (gap S1-6 (G4)). It also copies the inner preference (preference-rank, S1-3 (G1)). This rule is missing from the inventory.

rules.name: partial-bind-known
rules.derives: Cost::bind_known binds a directive cost and, when a Sum or Maximum has unresolved quantities, keeps the sum or max of only the resolvable children. The caller marks the node with a SizeRelation unknown.
side_conditions: only Sum/Maximum roots decompose; other shapes become fully unknown
used for @perf O(...) statements (walker.rs:452-491) and function directives
rules.evidence: [S1] The kept children are asserted costs, and the dropped ones are recorded as an unknown, so the partial cost is a floor of asserted contributions. This belongs to the directive rules (I) but lives in cost.rs and is missing from the inventory. It needs a rule name, and asserted marking under §4.7 and §5.6.

rules.name: preference-rank
rules.derives: Part::max ranks parts Absent(0) < Cold(1) < Unmarked(2) < Hot(3) and, when ranks differ, keeps the higher-ranked part and discards the other's cost regardless of magnitude. Absent parts are made Unmarked by executed()/sibling(), and cost::nest copies the inner part's preference onto the multiplied result.
side_conditions: assumed but not established: a part left Absent carries no work (cost 1)
cost_of_loop calls executed() on the multiplied body only when no escape channel is present (walker.rs:1622-1626)
nest keeps inner.preference while setting cost = factor * inner.cost (cost.rs:2180-2190)
rules.evidence: [S1] Unsound under §2 and against §3.2. A loop whose body has no Normal-channel part (for example because a nested budget-cancelled loop moved its work to the Return channel) is multiplied by nest into an Absent part of cost factor*1. That part stays Absent because the loop has an escape channel, and the next Part::max against any Unmarked part (Reading::total at function level) discards it. Counterexample (confirmed): `export function prefRank(n: number, xs: number[], ys: number[]): number { if (n >= 0 && n <= 1000000000) { let i = 0, total = 0; for (const x of xs) { for (const y of ys) { while (i < n && i >= 0) { i++; total += y; } } } return total; } return 0; }` reports O(n) Known while its work is Theta(xs*ys) for n = 1. The shipped test `a while under two enclosing loops` (tests/integration/budgets.rs:596-601) already asserts O(N) complete for this shape, whose true work is n*|xs| test evaluations. Gap S1-3 (G1). Verified (amended): The ledger counterexample does not reproduce as written: without range guards on the counter (i >= 0 and a bounded endpoint) olint leaves the loop bound unresolved, so the defective path is never taken. The guarded prefRank reports O(n) Known (trace: while [budget: i < n] x n only), with Theta(|xs|*|ys|) iterator steps, so the Absent-drop in Part::max (cost.rs:1800-1863), nest keeping the Absent preference (cost.rs:2189) and walker.rs:1623-1626 are confirmed; the shipped test at tests/integration/budgets.rs:596-601 shows the same loss. Reproduced with target/debug/olint.exe (built 15:06 from the working tree, whose analysis semantics match HEAD ce0cb54: the diff only adds snapshot recording and assertion counters) on refute-1/src/index.ts; outputs in refute-1/report.txt and refute-1/lint.txt.

rules.name: product-normalise
rules.derives: Sum/Product/Maximum combine flattens same-kind children, folds constants (add, multiply, max), collapses a product containing constant 0 with otherwise valid factors to 0, groups equal product factors into powers, rewrites N*log N to the legacy N log N atom and sorts by structural key.
side_conditions: checked arithmetic on constants (Overflow error)
node, depth and text budgets (Resource error); a resource failure becomes a ResourceExhaustion unknown at the caller
rules.evidence: [S1] Algebraic identities on nonnegative reals. The zero-collapse (cost.rs:319-321) makes a cost literally 0, which is not an upper bound on work of at least one operation unless the model reads O(0) as O(1). This semantic choice has to be fixed in the Lean model (gap S1-9 (G49)). [S7 tests, compliant] Exact Cost values asserted for products, ratios, exponents, logs.

rules.name: seq-max
rules.derives: A statement sequence (and any node whose children are evaluated in turn) costs the per-channel maximum of its members' readings: Reading::merge joins each (phase, completion) channel with Part::max.
side_conditions: the number of merged members is a program constant (syntax children), so a sum of that many terms is Theta of their maximum
channels are keyed by (phase, completion); a member's escape channel is joined only with the same escape channel of the others (cost.rs:1973-1996, 2032-2056)
after an await that definitely suspends, later statements move to the Scheduled phase; a possibly suspending statement joins both phases with an UnsupportedModel unknown (walker.rs:686-737, 757-770)
rules.evidence: [S1] Sound as an asymptotic rule: a fixed number of summands is at most that count times their max, and the per-channel split never drops work because Reading::total takes the max over every non-lazy channel (cost.rs:2101-2112). Gap only for §6.1/§6.4/§6.5: no rule name, side conditions or certificate. The Absent-rank selection inside Part::max, which this rule shares, is recorded under preference-rank. [S7 tests, compliant] Exact Cost/Part equality asserted in cost.test.rs; walker tests assert exact totals for sibling selection.

rules.name: bound-additive
rules.derives: For c moving toward a stable endpoint e with every advance >= 0, a guaranteed per-iteration advance g > 0 and float headroom, factor = max(cost(initial), cost(e)) (quantity_maximum).
side_conditions: all advances numeric (else Unresolved); replacing writes on a driven counter give Unresolved
is_stable_endpoint: no call/new/await/yield/assignment/function in e and no write reference inside the loop to any binding e mentions
initial and endpoint are bounded quantities; some unconditional delta survives rounding at the larger magnitude (bounds.rs:990-995)
rules.evidence: [S1] Iterations <= |e - initial|/g + 1 = O(max(cost)) with g a program constant, and the headroom check rules out a stalled i++ near 2^53. Endpoint stability ignores member writes (`o.x`) and aliasing, which effects invalidation covers instead (S1-10 (G54)).

rules.name: bound-best-of
rules.derives: Among the comparisons in the test's &&-conjuncts, keeps the verdict of lowest strength (1 < LOG < other proven < Unresolved).
side_conditions: each conjunct is necessary for another iteration
rules.evidence: [S1] Any conjunct's bound bounds the conjunction. Ties among non-LOG proven bounds keep the first, not the smallest (a lost tightening, not unsound). [S7 tests, compliant] Unit test pins strength ordering; integration pins distinct endpoints.

rules.name: bound-bisection
rules.derives: `lo < hi` (or <=) where every write to lo and hi in the loop is an assignment of a truncated midpoint (+1 for lo, +0/-1 for hi), on every path, with nonnegative initials of magnitude <= 2^30: factor LOG ('halving').
side_conditions: no deferred or update writes; no continue to head; midpoint forms (lo+hi)>>1, floor((lo+hi)/2), lo + ((hi-lo)>>1)
magnitude cap prevents int32 overflow in >>
rules.evidence: [S1] Each iteration at least halves hi - lo. Sound. The cap rejects Array-length initials (magnitude 2^32-1 > 2^30), which is conservative. Certificate needed. [S7 tests, compliant] Pinned (whileHalvingMidpoint).

rules.name: bound-constant-collection
rules.derives: for-of over a constant-sized collection: factor 1, proof 'constant collection'.
side_conditions: cardinality_of(right) == Constant (constants.rs/value_sizes.rs)
rules.evidence: [S1] Sound if constant-cardinality (H) is sound. Gap for §6.1/§6.4/§6.5.

rules.name: bound-constant-distance
rules.derives: When initial and endpoint are numeric, or the endpoint is the initial plus or minus a numeric offset, factor 1 with proof 'constant bound' or 'constant offset from start'.
side_conditions: same preconditions as bound-additive; distance/g + 1 finite
rules.evidence: [S1] Sound under bound-additive's preconditions. The offset form uses is_same_reading on member paths, so it depends on S1-10 (G54) for member writes inside the loop. Gap for §6.1/§6.4/§6.5. [S7 tests, compliant] Pinned with reason labels.

rules.name: bound-directive
rules.derives: @perf bounded on a loop gives factor 1 with proof '@perf bounded' (and counts an assertion in the working tree).
side_conditions: directive present on the loop
rules.evidence: [S1] Asserted per §3.3. Needs asserted marking in the explanation and report (§4.7, §5.6) and a rule name (§6.5). Otherwise directive-owned (family I). [S7 tests, compliant] Model fixture asserts boundedLoopStatement reads "@perf bounded" (bounds.rs:71).

rules.name: bound-exact-additive
rules.derives: With some backward advance but every write unconditional, not deferred and outside nested loops, numeric initial/endpoint/deltas in quarter units, and magnitude <= 2^48: factor 1 ('constant bound').
side_conditions: guaranteed (net) advance > 0 was established earlier (bounds.rs:955-967)
rules.evidence: [S1] Every write runs exactly once per iteration, so the net advance per iteration is the guaranteed g > 0. Quarter-unit exactness within 2^48 makes the float arithmetic exact. Sound; certificate needed.

rules.name: bound-false-condition
rules.derives: A while/for/do-while whose test is the literal false: factor 1.
side_conditions: test is BooleanLiteral(false) after unwrapping
rules.evidence: [S1] Sound (0 iterations, or 1 for do-while). Gap for §6.1/§6.4/§6.5 only. [S7 tests, compliant] bounds.rs:955-970 asserts while(false), for(;false;), do..while(false) known and O(1); coverage sits inside a test named for a different rule.

rules.name: bound-for-in
rules.derives: for-in over a constant-sized or closed-type object: factor 1 ('closed object type'); otherwise factor Cost::N with no proof label.
side_conditions: is_constant_sized or is_closed (closed object type)
rules.evidence: [S1] Non-closed for-in claims N iterations, the input envelope, with no tie to the object's key count. That is an assumption outside §2 (§2.1). Counterexample (node level): `export function q(xs: number[]): number { const o: Record<string, number> = {}; for (const a of xs) for (const b of xs) o[`${a},${b}`] = 1; let c = 0; for (const k in o) c++; return c; }`. The for-in node claims O(N) (N bound to xs), while it enumerates Theta(xs^2) keys. Closed-type factor 1 is sound. Gap S1-7 (G5). [S7 tests, compliant] Model fixture forInClosed/forInRecord read "N"; bounds.rs:89 loop; values.rs:240-274 prototype cases.

rules.name: bound-for-of-native
rules.derives: A for-of over native iteration gets factor = iteration_count_of(right) with no proof label, after the live-visits, constant and share checks.
side_conditions: iteration_count_of returns a count (invocations.rs), else Unresolved
live_iteration_of not Unresolved
rules.evidence: [S1] The count's derivation is in invocations.rs (iterator-visits, E, slice 2). Where that count is the input envelope Cost::N, the envelope gap applies (S1-7 (G5), plan 'Size envelope'). [S7 tests, compliant] Model fixture forOfTuple reads "N"; native iterable acquisition asserted with exact costs.

rules.name: bound-geometric
rules.derives: All counter writes geometric with numeric ratios. Upward: ratios > 1 and numeric initial >= 1. Downward: |ratio| <= 0.5 and numeric endpoint clearing 0. Either gives factor LOG ('geometric step'/'halving'). A shift-left write gives Unresolved.
side_conditions: at least one unconditional write; initial and endpoint bounded quantities; stable endpoint
rules.evidence: [S1] log-many iterations up to the endpoint magnitude. The factor is legacy LOG, bound to log of the envelope rather than log of the endpoint quantity, so it inherits the envelope convention (S1-7 (G5)/S1-9 (G49)). The downward strict-0 case terminates only through IEEE-754 underflow, so its soundness rests on double semantics (S1-11 (G50)).

rules.name: bound-iterator-visits
rules.derives: A for-of over non-native (user iterator/generator) iteration gets factor = the iterator's visit count, proof 'iterator visits'.
side_conditions: iteration.native is false; count from iteration_count_of
rules.evidence: [S1] Soundness depends on the E-family iterator-visits derivation (invocations.rs:743-775). Gap for §6.1/§6.4/§6.5. [S7 tests, compliant] Exact cost and completeness asserted.

rules.name: bound-linear-default
rules.derives: A loop kind with no body or an unexpected kind gets linear_bound_of() = Cost::N.
side_conditions: none
rules.evidence: [S1] Reachable only for malformed iteration kinds (every iteration statement has a body), so it is effectively dead. If reached, it is an envelope assumption (S1-7 (G5)). This rule is missing from the inventory.

rules.name: bound-live-visits
rules.derives: for-of over a Set/Map identifier that the body grows under a size guard gets factor max(N, budget.cost), proof 'visit budget'; an unresolved live classification gives Unresolved.
side_conditions: live_iteration_of classifies Budgeted via size-guarded additions (effects.rs, budgets.rs:1031-1149)
N stands for the collection's initial size
rules.evidence: [S1] The initial-size term is the input envelope Cost::N, not the collection's size, which is an assumption outside §2 (§2.1). Counterexample (node level): `export function s(xs: number[], cap: number): number { const set = new Set<number>(); for (const a of xs) for (const b of xs) set.add(a * 65536 + b); let c = 0; for (const v of set) { if (set.size < cap) set.add(-v); c++; } return c; }`. The last for-of claims max(N, cap-budget) visits, while its work is Theta(xs^2) with N bound to the xs envelope. Gap S1-7 (G5). [S7 tests, compliant] Pinned (includes Set/Map cases).

rules.name: bound-progression
rules.derives: Classifies each write to the loop counter inside the loop span (additive/geometric/replacing step, deferred into a nested function, in the for-update) and which writes execute on every body path (covers_every_path / covers_sequence / skips_remainder).
side_conditions: only writes whose reference span lies inside the loop are seen (write_sites_of); writes through closures defined outside, aliases or member paths are not seen here and are left to loop-effect-invalidation
a path that leaves the iteration covers vacuously; a continue to the loop head or a break inside the body not covering the write defeats coverage
conditional expressions cover only when both arms cover; logical operators never cover
rules.evidence: [S1] The path-coverage analysis is conservative in every case checked (switch, try, logical, nested loop and deferred writes never count as unconditional). Its soundness for counter writes outside the loop span depends on effects.rs invalidation (gap S1-10 (G54)). This rule is missing from the inventory as a separate step.

rules.name: bound-quantity
rules.derives: bounded_quantity_of gives an expression a (cost, magnitude) pair: numeric literal, sum/difference, Array/String length, const alias, or a value guarded in the loop test (and by enclosing if-tests whose bindings are only written in the loop) between a numeric lower bound >= 0 and a bounded upper bound <= 2^53. The cost comes from substitutions, parameter value quantities, the collection length, the upper bound's cost, or a guarded initial.
side_conditions: outside the test: no write to any referenced local binding (or none inside the loop for the for-init)
memoised per proof with cycle detection (QuantityProof)
rules.evidence: [S1] The magnitude ceilings keep float progress sound. The cost it assigns is the dimension of the bounding quantity. Soundness of parameter_quantity_of and the substitution sizes is H/E (slices 2 and 3). Gap for §6.1/§6.4/§6.5.

rules.name: bound-share
rules.derives: A for statement `c < e` with c initialised in the for-init, e share-sized (or initial + share), and c advancing at least 1 per iteration gets factor 1, proof 'share of budget'. A for-of over a share-sized collection gets the same.
side_conditions: e and the initial are bounded quantities with float headroom
is_share_sized(e) against the active share_bindings
consumes_a_unit: every advance >= 0 and guaranteed advance >= 1
rules.evidence: [S1] Factor 1 per visit is justified only by amortisation against the enclosing budget (budget-share), and that amortisation omits the final overshooting share, so the bound is unsound. Counterexample under budget-share (gap S1-5 (G3)). Confirmed with the guarded counterexample recorded under budget-share: the inner for gets factor 1 ("share of budget") and the entry reports O(n) Known. Verified (amended): Upheld as non-compliant; evidence amended to point at a counterexample that reproduces (see budget-share). bounds.rs:316-317 (HEAD 314-315) returns constant_bound_of("share of budget"). Reproduced with target/debug/olint.exe (built 15:06 from the working tree, whose analysis semantics match HEAD ce0cb54: the diff only adds snapshot recording and assertion counters) on refute-1/src/index.ts; outputs in refute-1/report.txt and refute-1/lint.txt. [S7 tests, compliant] Pinned with positive and negative cases.

rules.name: bound-single-iteration
rules.derives: A loop whose body's completion always leaves the iteration (return, throw, break of this or an outer target, continue of an outer loop) and that has no continue to its own head runs at most once: factor 1.
side_conditions: flow::completion_of(body) is Some and leaves_iteration
returns_to_head is false (no continue targeting this loop in the body, including nested loops, excluding nested functions)
rules.evidence: [S1] Sound given flow-completion: every normal path through the body ends in a transfer out of the loop. Gap for §6.1/§6.4/§6.5 only. [S7 tests, compliant] Label and negative case pinned.

rules.name: for-of-produced-length
rules.derives: For a for-of whose factor is Cost::N, a produced size that exceeds N replaces the factor with its length. An unresolved produced length adds a SizeRelation unknown as a sibling but keeps factor N on the body.
side_conditions: produced_size_of(right) (values.rs)
rules.evidence: [S1] When the length is unresolved, the body*N contribution stays presented as proven with N the input envelope. The unknown is a separate sibling, not the multiplicity, so the rule relies on the envelope assumption outside §2 (§2.1). Replacing N by a proven produced length is sound. Gap S1-7 (G5).

rules.name: loop-effect-invalidation
rules.derives: Header and body call effects, plus pending async interference, decide invalidation.bound (the loop's own bound is untrusted) and invalidation.budget (the budget context is withheld from the body).
side_conditions: effects of calls in test/update/body and for-of iteration; header storage and budget storage (effects.rs:1888-1968, 2069-2185)
header effects (while/do-while test, for test and update, for-of iteration protocol) carry no unknown_global and no unknown_reachable (effects.rs:825-859)
joined body+header effects do not write any header binding, have no unclassified write on it, and write no member value that is or may alias a header value (effects.rs:1888-1972)
for a Set/Map for-of, live visits classify as Stable{written} or Budgeted so the iterated value is skipped from header storage (effects.rs:849-857, 1986-1988)
for loops in async functions or async generators that suspend, pending effects of scheduled work in the owner plus key interference do not affect header or budget storage (effects.rs:902-991)
budget storage of the loop is unaffected by the same effects (effects.rs:1912-1915)
rules.evidence: [S1] Cross-reference: effects.rs is slice 6's. This rule carries the side conditions that bounds.rs and budgets.rs leave out (writes through closures, aliases and members), so certificates for bound-* and budget-* must cite it (S1-10 (G54)). [S6] No named proof rule, recorded side conditions, certificate or Lean soundness theorem (§6.1, §6.4, §6.5). Soundness direction is conservative (invalidation only removes proofs). Scaling: each loop re-runs the effect prepass over its entire body subtree with no per-loop cache, so a depth-d loop nest costs Theta(d^2) EffectPrepassNode (S6-9 (G71)); invalidation_of walks all ancestors per loop (effects.rs:1902-1909); affects() scans member_writes x storage.values with may_alias uncharged (effects.rs:1956-1964); Effects::join is a quadratic Vec::contains merge (effects.rs:359-379, S6-8 (G72)); pending_invalidation_of runs twice for live Set/Map for-of loops (effects.rs:861, 884-886) and charges pending.weight*effects.weight (effects.rs:940-943). [S7 tests, compliant] Pinned with negative and positive cases.

rules.name: loop-nest
rules.derives: A loop with a proven non-unit factor f contributes nest(f, body Normal part per phase) to the Normal channel, or to the scope/Return channel when budget-cancelled. Escape channels of the body are joined without multiplication, and escapes absorbed at this loop join Normal once.
side_conditions: bound proven and not invalidated (invalidation.bound false or @perf bounded)
multiplied part is marked executed only when no escape channel is present (walker.rs:1623-1626)
rules.evidence: [S1] f * body is a sound bound when f bounds the iteration count. The `escaped` exception to executed() feeds the Absent-drop defect (preference-rank, S1-3 (G1)). The loop proof label is one &'static str (bounds.rs:60-64), so the side conditions go unrecorded (§6.5, S1-2 (G48)). [S7 tests, compliant] Exact cost assertions.

rules.name: loop-phases
rules.derives: A loop's header children split into once-evaluated siblings (for-init, for-of/for-in iterable, iterator acquire/close, consumed latent) and repeated visits (test, update, for-of/for-in binding, iterator next). Visits are merged into the body before multiplication; siblings are joined outside it.
side_conditions: LoopPhases::repeats marks test, binding and update (flow.rs:1103-1105)
the test's extra final evaluation is absorbed because factor >= 1
rules.evidence: [S1] Matches ECMAScript loop evaluation. This rule is missing from the inventory. It interacts with budget-cancel, which moves the visit cost out of the per-visit account (gap S1-4 (G2)).

rules.name: loop-suspension
rules.derives: In an async context whose loop body suspends and whose factor is not 1, the body's Immediate Normal part retains an UnsupportedModel unknown and is also joined into the Scheduled phase.
side_conditions: is_async_context and suspends(body)
rules.evidence: [S1] Conservative (duplicates work across phases and marks Partial). Gap for §6.1/§6.4/§6.5.

rules.name: loop-unbounded
rules.derives: A loop whose bound is unresolved or invalidated (and not @perf bounded) contributes its body Normal part once with unknowns scaled by an unknown factor, plus a Bound (or resolver-supplied) unknown at the loop, maxed with absorbed escapes. The factor defaults to Cost::N for the other computations.
side_conditions: invalidation.bound from effects.rs or an unresolved bound
note_unresolved_multiplicity forgets recurrence multiplicity when the body mentions recurrence dimensions
rules.evidence: [S1] The Partial cost counts the body once, so it presents body cost as a proven contribution. A body constituent's contribution includes its multiplicity (Terms: Contribution), which is unknown here, and the spec floor joins proven contributions only (Terms: Floor). Instances iterating k times exceed that claim. Lint fails on the printed cost (main.rs:328-334), giving Exceeds verdicts §4.2 does not license. Counterexample (confirmed): `export function unbounded(xs: number[]): number { let c = 0; let k = 1; while (k !== xs.length) { for (const a of xs) for (const b of xs) c += a * b; k = (k * 3) % 7; } return c; }` with max O(N) reports `O(xs^2) [partial] > O(N)` and lint exits 1, though no contribution of cost xs^2 is proven. Also, `granted` (share) is computed with the default factor N even when the bound is unresolved (walker.rs:1424-1431). Gap S1-6 (G4). Verified (amended): Defect upheld: walker.rs:1577-1606 keeps body_main.cost after scaled(None) (cost.rs:1706-1711 scales only the unknowns), and main.rs:326-334 counts it as Exceeds. The ledger counterexample h(xs, p: () => boolean) does not fail lint: its comparison against O(N) is Inconclusive (olint prints "unknown comparison for ... against O(N)"), apparently because the function-typed parameter leaves the limit comparison unresolved. Replaced with a counterexample whose loop bound is unresolved without a function parameter; it fails lint. The granted-from-default-N point (walker.rs:1389, 1424-1431) is confirmed by the code. Reproduced with target/debug/olint.exe (built 15:06 from the working tree, whose analysis semantics match HEAD ce0cb54: the diff only adds snapshot recording and assertion counters) on refute-1/src/index.ts; outputs in refute-1/report.txt and refute-1/lint.txt. [S7 tests, compliant] Pinned as unresolved; but see S7-4 (G4): the partial cost counts test/body work once under unknown multiplicity.

rules.name: loop-unit
rules.derives: A loop whose proven factor is 1 contributes max(body, absorbed escapes) without multiplication.
side_conditions: factor.is_one() from a constant bound
rules.evidence: [S1] Sound: the body runs a bounded constant number of times. Gap for §6.1/§6.4/§6.5 only. [S7 tests, compliant] Exact cost and label assertions per loop phase.

rules.name: budget-cancel
rules.derives: A loop spending a constant-step budget (every write to the counter a proven constant step), with factor >= potential (and visits <= factor for do-while), sends factor*body to pending_scoped[scope], or to the Return channel when inside a loop, so enclosing loops below the scope do not multiply it.
side_conditions: spend found in the for-update or a top-level expression statement of the body; the loop is one the budget's condition guards; no continue at body level
charge_covers(factor, potential), and charge_covers(factor, visits) only for do-while (budgets.rs:145-147, walker.rs:1519-1528)
budget context withheld when invalidation.budget
rules.evidence: [S1] Only the body executions are amortised against the potential. Each visit also evaluates the test (and for-of next) at least once, and that per-visit header work is folded into body_main (walker.rs:1446-1448) and so moved out of the enclosing multiplication. Counterexample (confirmed): `function sum(xs: readonly number[]): number { let s = 0; for (const x of xs) s += x; return s; } export function cancelHeader(n: number, m: number, xs: number[]): number { if (n >= 0 && n <= 1000000000 && m >= 0 && m <= 1000000000) { let i = 0, c = 0; for (let j = 0; j < n; j++) { while (sum(xs) > j && i < m && i >= 0) { i++; c++; } } return c; } return 0; }` reports O(m*xs) Known, while the n visits each evaluate sum(xs) once: Theta(n*xs) for m = 1. Using the Return channel as the no-multiply device also produces the Absent parts that preference-rank drops (S1-3 (G1)). Gap S1-4 (G2). Verified (amended): Defect upheld: walker.rs:1446-1448 merges the header (visit) reading into body_raw, and the cancelled loop is nested once by its factor (walker.rs:1622, 1636-1657) and then not multiplied by the enclosing loop. The ledger counterexample does not reproduce: with xs.includes(j) and an unguarded i < ys.length the while bound is unresolved (unknown iteration bound), so no cancellation happens. Replaced with a guarded counterexample whose header calls a local O(xs) function. Reproduced with target/debug/olint.exe (built 15:06 from the working tree, whose analysis semantics match HEAD ce0cb54: the diff only adds snapshot recording and assertion counters) on refute-1/src/index.ts; outputs in refute-1/report.txt and refute-1/lint.txt. [S7 tests, compliant] Pinned. Assertions state the O-class; no certificate check exists (see S7-7 (G58)).

rules.name: budget-collect
rules.derives: A budget per counter binding: a non-var local with numeric initial compared in a while/do-while/for test against a bound invariant in the function, with all writes in the function monotone one way. Potential = |numeric endpoint - initial|, else the bound's size or collection length, else Enveloped (Cost::N). Scope = the enclosing iteration of the declaration.
side_conditions: writes_of and is_invariant scan the function body excluding nested functions (counted_subtree skips them)
mutator calls and delete on a binding count as writes; writes through aliases or closures are left to effects invalidation
rules.evidence: [S1] The potential argument (a monotone counter crosses at most |endpoint - initial| units) is sound when effects invalidation covers closure and alias writes (S1-10 (G54)). Potential::Enveloped is the envelope (S1-7 (G5)), but it only enables cancellation when the loop factor is proven >= N. [S7 tests, compliant] Pinned by positive/negative budget tests.

rules.name: budget-share
rules.derives: A loop spending a budget by a stable identifier k (`i += k`) grants k as a share binding for its body when visits*factor covers the potential. While granted, loops bounded by k get factor 1 (bound-share), and share-sized operations lose their linear cost (share-sized-operation).
side_conditions: k is a const identifier binding or an unwritten identifier parameter
visits_since(scope) * factor covers potential (walker.rs:1424-1431), where factor may be the default N of an unresolved bound
rules.evidence: [S1] The sum of shares over a visit is bounded by the potential plus the last share, which overshoots past the endpoint. Counterexample (confirmed): `export function shareOvershoot(n: number, m: number): number { if (n >= 0 && n <= 1000000000 && m >= 1 && m <= 1000000000) { let i = 0, steps = 0, t = 0; while (i < n && i >= 0 && steps < n && steps >= 0) { const k = m; for (let j = 0; j < k; j++) t++; i += k; steps++; } return t; } return 0; }`. Budget i has potential n, the while's factor is n, k is granted, the inner for gets factor 1 ('share of budget'), and olint reports O(n) Known. With n = 1 and m = M the inner loop runs M times: Theta(M). Gap S1-5 (G3). Verified (amended): The ledger counterexample does not reproduce as written: without range guards on the counter (i >= 0 and a bounded endpoint) olint leaves the loop bound unresolved, so the defective path is never taken. The guarded shareOvershoot reports O(n) Known (while [budget: i < n, by k] x n), confirming the overshoot. The "k >= 1 is never established" point is dropped: a share below 1 costs at most one inner iteration per visit, which the loop factor already covers because granting requires visits*factor to cover the potential, so it is no separate unsoundness. Reproduced with target/debug/olint.exe (built 15:06 from the working tree, whose analysis semantics match HEAD ce0cb54: the diff only adds snapshot recording and assertion counters) on refute-1/src/index.ts; outputs in refute-1/report.txt and refute-1/lint.txt.

rules.name: hoisted-join
rules.derives: Parts cancelled against a budget scoped to an enclosing loop wait in pending_scoped and join that loop's body per phase before its multiplication. Hot/cold statements re-prefer their pending scoped parts.
side_conditions: scope is an ancestor loop; the scope loop's factor multiplies the hoisted part once per scope iteration
rules.evidence: [S1] Correct placement of scoped amortised work. It inherits budget-cancel's lost per-visit header work for loops between the cancelled loop and its scope (S1-4 (G2)). [S7 tests, gap] Only incidental coverage: no test targets the pending_scoped hoisted join of walker.rs:1488-1497 by name or by an exact hoisted cost.

rules.name: share-sized-operation
rules.derives: While a share binding is active, a linear constructor with a share-sized first argument, a native array/Set/Map method on a share-sized receiver (or set with a share-sized argument, or subarray/slice(0, share)) and a for-of over a share-sized collection cost only their callback (or nothing) instead of length*callback.
side_conditions: is_share_sized: share binding, const alias, share + numeric constant, subarray/slice(0, share) or (a, a + share)
rules.evidence: [S1] Rests on the same amortisation as budget-share and inherits the last-share overshoot: a share-sized receiver makes `bounded` true (walker.rs:2694-2708), so the linear operation is charged nothing per visit, and the constructor path (walker.rs:2071-2082) charges nothing for a share-sized length. The callback reading is left unmultiplied by the length (walker.rs:2754-2755), which is the same amortisation a share-sized for loop receives (factor 1 times body), so it is covered by, not separate from, the overshoot defect. This rule is missing from the inventory. Gap S1-5 (G3). Verified (amended): Non-compliance upheld through the overshoot inherited from budget-share. The separate claim that dropping the callback length multiplier is an extra defect is refuted: a share-sized loop body is charged once per enclosing iteration too (share-of-budget factor 1), and the budget amortises the total of the shares, so callback*k summed over iterations is at most (potential + overshoot)*callback, as in the loop case. Fixing the overshoot fixes both.

rules.name: escape-absorb
rules.derives: At a loop, break/continue escapes that exit this loop but not its enclosing loop join the loop's Normal channel once (not multiplied). Other escapes pass through unmultiplied.
side_conditions: exits_iteration and absorbs_escape against enclosing_iteration_of
rules.evidence: [S1] A lifted escape runs once per run of the absorbing loop, and outer loops then multiply it by their factors. Sound. Gap for §6.1/§6.4/§6.5.

rules.name: escape-depth-exhausted
rules.derives: Escape resolution deeper than MAXIMUM_ESCAPE_DEPTH (32) leaves the reading in Normal (multiplied) and adds a ResourceExhaustion unknown.
side_conditions: depth counter through finalizer replacements
rules.evidence: [S1] Conservative fallback that marks the node Partial. Under §7.4 it should be justified by a scaling family. Gap for §6.1/§6.4/§6.5. [S7 tests, compliant] Pinned as linear work and partial; the partial result caused by a depth cap contradicts spec 7.4 (see S7-5 (G67)).

rules.name: escape-lift
rules.derives: The Normal work of a branch that always completes abruptly moves to its resolved escape channel ('runs once per loop/call') when every transfer in the branch escapes the enclosing iteration. A return/throw argument's work moves to the resolved escape channel. try/catch/finally interceptions weaken or cancel the escape.
side_conditions: flow::completion_of(branch) is Some (every normal path ends in a transfer)

every transfer in the branch that does not target inside it resolves (escape_of_completion) to an escape of the enclosing iteration; a continue to the loop itself or a handler inside the loop yields None (no lift)
finalizer transfers replace the escape; unresolved finalizers weaken to Break(try)
rules.evidence: [S1] The cases checked are sound: a continue in the middle of the branch, a handler catching inside the loop, a finally overriding with continue, labelled continue of an outer loop, and a throw caught by a try between loops (the escape weakens to Break(try) and is absorbed at the inner loop). Gap for §6.1/§6.4/§6.5. [S7 tests, compliant] Exact costs and targets asserted.

rules.name: flow-completion
rules.derives: completion_of: return/throw/break/continue resolve their targets. A block completes as its last statement. An if with both arms abrupt completes as the nearer (weaker) of the two. Everything else is None (may complete normally).
side_conditions: control_target_of resolves labels and unlabelled break/continue within the function; interceptions_of lists enclosing try handlers and finalizers
rules.evidence: [S1] Under-approximates abrupt completion (labelled statements, switch and try give None), which is the safe direction for bound-single-iteration, bound-progression and escape-lift. This rule is missing from the inventory. Gap for §6.1/§6.4/§6.5.

rules.name: flow-graph
rules.derives: FlowContext::build builds a per-function flow graph (points, guarded edges, completion actions, exits), and FlowIndex a child index.
rules.evidence: [S1] No analysis path calls SourceFile::flow/flow_with_limit/flow_context or FlowContext::build (only src/flow.test.rs and tests/integration/flow.rs do); FlowSummary, FlowFailure, the Builder and LoopPhases::iterates (called only by Builder::loop_flow) serve only that graph. The per-file FlowIndex (project.rs:1605) is contributing: SourceFile::children_of (project.rs:76-78) reads it, and walker, budgets, effects, summaries and public_surface call children_of. The analysis-time cost of the dead graph is the oxc control-flow graph that project.rs:1579 requests with with_cfg(true), which only flow.rs:203 and flow.rs:312 read. completion_of, control_target_of, Completion, Resumption and loop_phases_of in flow.rs are used and stay. Gap S1-8 (G85). Verified (amended): Non-contributing status upheld for the flow-graph builder and its SourceFile entry points (git grep at HEAD finds no caller outside the two test files). Refuted in part: the FlowIndex built at project.rs:1605 backs SourceFile::children_of, which the walker uses on every loop and statement, so it is contributing and stays. The wasted §7 time is instead the with_cfg(true) CFG construction at project.rs:1579 and the oxc_cfg dependency, which only the dead builder reads. Locations corrected accordingly.

rules.name: async-assimilation
rules.derives: Awaiting or resolving with a value invokes its then getter immediately and its then callbacks (program-defined, resolved through descriptors) in the Scheduled phase with resolve/reject settlers; an intrinsic promise with no replaced then contributes nothing; open then targets add a Scheduled Target unknown.
side_conditions: primitive operands contribute nothing (invocations.rs:2628-2630)
is_intrinsic_promise with no then accessor or method in the program's index contributes nothing (invocations.rs:2635-2646)
assimilation nesting depth at most 6 and no re-entry at the same node, else ResourceExhaustion (summaries.rs:6211-6215)
open values add a Target unknown unless the proven kind is built-in (invocations.rs:2717-2734)
rules.evidence: [S2] Input thenables are covered: open then values on unresolved receivers add a Scheduled Target unknown (invocations.rs:2717-2734), so f(p: PromiseLike<number>) and f(p: Promise<number>) are Partial. A `then` getter on an external value is closed by the program-only accessor index (invocations.rs:2633), but only inside a node the Target unknown already makes Partial. No certificate or rule name (§6.1, §6.4, §6.5; S2-1 (G46)). Verified (refuted): The counterexample is already covered. For a non-intrinsic operand property_values_of on an input receiver is open and proven_kind is Unknown, so assimilated_reading_of adds a Scheduled Target unknown (invocations.rs:2717-2734); p1 `g(p: PromiseLike<number>)` and p2 `g(p: Promise<number>)` both report O(1) [partial] with an unknown call target at the await. The residual omission is a `then` getter on an external value (property_accessors_of closed when the program defines no `then` accessor, invocations.rs:2633), whose node is already Partial through the Target unknown at the same await origin, so no Known bound is violated. The rule remains a gap for certification only (S2-1 (G46)). Checked with the working-tree debug build (target/debug/olint.exe, copied to .scratch/olint-compliance/refute-2/) over refute-2/p1..p5 with --types syntactic --min 0; the working-tree edits touch asserted/snapshot recording, not these paths.

rules.name: await-continuation
rules.derives: Statements after an await that definitely suspends move to the Scheduled phase and run once as scheduled work; an await that may suspend joins both phases with an UnsupportedModel unknown.
rules.evidence: [merge] No code slice mapped this inventory rule separately; like every rule it applies with no rule name, recorded side conditions, certificate or soundness theorem (G46). Status gap for certification only.

rules.name: call-callback-parameter
rules.derives: A callback value created from a known function expression, declaration or pattern-bound function carries a descriptor (function, captured substitutions, storage, generation); invoking it re-enters the call path with those captures plus supplied parameter parts, and an open target set adds a Target unknown.
side_conditions: the descriptor's generation equals the scheduler generation, else Target unknown (summaries.rs:3308-3310)
captured substitutions are the parameter facts of enclosing functions of the target (summaries.rs:2739-2785)
a value without a descriptor falls back to its explicit callback part or a Target unknown (summaries.rs:3372-3379)
supplied parts bind only plain identifier parameters (summaries.rs:3409-3439)
PromiseResolve descriptors invoked implicitly are Target unknowns; invoked explicitly they assimilate the first argument (summaries.rs:3313-3320)
rules.evidence: [S2] Sound as far as read: unknown descriptors and open targets degrade to unknowns. No certificate or rule name (§6.1, §6.4, §6.5).

rules.name: call-effects-transfer
rules.derives: A callee's recorded effects (binding writes, storage, escapes, unknown reach) enter the caller with the callee's parameter values replaced by the argument storage values; storage arguments propagate into the specialisation key. These effects feed loop-effect-invalidation, so they decide which loop bounds survive.
side_conditions: substitution applies only to write-free plain identifier parameters and stops at the first pattern parameter (summaries.rs:4282-4303)
effects with unknown_global are not substituted (summaries.rs:4274-4276)
writes to bindings declared within the callee are dropped (summaries.rs:798-800)
rules.evidence: [S2] Missing from the inventory, and it affects costs indirectly through effects.rs invalidation. No certificate (§6.1, §6.4).

rules.name: call-fallback
rules.derives: When a task runs in fallback (budget exhausted), a call reuses the readings of the specialisations the parent task observed at the same site on earlier passes, merged; a closed top-level zero-parameter function reuses its closed Ready summary; anything else is a ResourceExhaustion unknown.
side_conditions: the observed set at (site, target) is non-empty and complete, and every observed task's interference equals the current interference, else a ResourceExhaustion unknown is retained (summaries.rs:4364-4395, 4411-4427)
closed_ready applies only to a top-level Function with no parameters, rest or this parameter, and a key with no substitutions, storage or interference (summaries.rs:1321-1329, 4495-4515)
an observed task still in the active component yields its local record with a ResourceExhaustion unknown (summaries.rs:4439-4449)
rules.evidence: [S2] Soundness rests on an unstated invariant: the fallback pass would compute one of the observed SummaryKeys at that site. Observations from a pass that later went Waiting or exhausted are kept, and the merge is a max over them, so the invariant is plausible but unproven (S2-16 (G56)). Uncertified (§6.1, §6.4). [S7 tests, compliant] Pinned; fallback results are resource-driven (see S7-5 (G67)).

rules.name: call-lazy-phase
rules.derives: A callee reading's Lazy channel (generator bodies, returned latent work) is dropped at a plain call (Excluded), moved to Immediate at a consuming call (Consumed), or moved to Immediate with a Multiplicity unknown when the value escapes (Escaped); Scheduled channels pass through.
side_conditions: every consumption of the latent value is charged where it happens, through lazy-consume, or an untracked consumption charges it at the call with a Multiplicity unknown (summaries.rs:5559-5577)
a Consumed call substitutes the stored deferred reading for the Lazy channel (summaries.rs:3808-3825, 4479-4493)
rules.evidence: [S2] Matches §1 Work (consumed lazy work only) provided lazy-consume's tracking predicate is complete; that premise is unproven and uncertified (§6.1, §6.4).

rules.name: call-open-remainder
rules.derives: A call whose target set is open keeps its known targets' readings and adds an unknown Target contribution for the open remainder.
rules.evidence: [merge] No code slice mapped this inventory rule separately; like every rule it applies with no rule name, recorded side conditions, certificate or soundness theorem (G46). Status gap for certification only.

rules.name: call-returned-function
rules.derives: A call to a function value returned by another call invokes the returned body with the callback facts and captures the returning call established (see returned-function-facts).
rules.evidence: [merge] No code slice mapped this inventory rule separately; like every rule it applies with no rule name, recorded side conditions, certificate or soundness theorem (G46). Status gap for certification only.

rules.name: call-summary
rules.derives: A call site's contribution is the callee's memoised summary reading for the specialisation key (function, argument facts, latent channels, storage arguments, interference, root sizes), re-bound into the caller's quantities; Ready summaries are reused, missing ones park the caller as Waiting and re-evaluate it once the dependency publishes.
side_conditions: key_of canonicalises every substitution (sorted targets, canonicalised latent effects, latent channel keys) so equal facts share a summary (summaries.rs:646-787)
the charged InvocationEvaluation, RuntimePair and InvocationSite admissions succeed, else the call is a ResourceExhaustion unknown (summaries.rs:3719-3764)
a dependency not yet Ready contributes Reading::empty() only on a pass that is discarded: the caller is marked Waiting and never publishes that pass (summaries.rs:1253-1262, 1491-1499)
at most specializations_per_function (32) keys per (function, raw, root sizes), else ResourceExhaustion unknown (summaries.rs:1078-1090)
callee effects are joined into the caller with parameter values substituted (summaries.rs:3800-3806)
the callee reading passes finish_reading, which binds every channel cost through bind_cost_in and turns a bind failure into cost_error plus an unknown (summaries.rs:556-590)
rules.evidence: [S2] No certificate, no named rule in the explanation (§6.1, §6.4, §6.5). The memoisation argument itself follows the key contents, but the bound it re-binds inherits size-substitution's envelope (S2-2 (G5)), and finish_reading mislabels bind failures as ResourceExhaustion (S2-13 (G35)). Evaluation order, and with it the number of body passes charged, follows HashSet iteration (S2-6 (G30)).

rules.name: construction-fields
rules.derives: A construction's cost includes the instance (and inherited) field initialisers of every class in its construction plan, cached per construction key (class, inherited flag, captured enclosing-parameter facts, storage, interference, root sizes).
side_conditions: a class already initialising on the stack yields a Recurrence unknown (summaries.rs:2611-2617, 2526-2543)
construction depth at most 32, else ResourceExhaustion (summaries.rs:2536-2538)
the cache stores a result only when no fallback, exhaustion, component, pending dependency, scoped pending, share binding or diagnostic change occurred (summaries.rs:2648-2661)
rules.evidence: [S2] Missing from the inventory. No certificate or rule name (§6.1, §6.4, §6.5).

rules.name: constructor-call
rules.derives: `new C(...)` costs the construction plan: the constructor body, instance field initialisers of every class in the lineage and base construction at `super` (see construction-fields).
rules.evidence: [merge] No code slice mapped this inventory rule separately; like every rule it applies with no rule name, recorded side conditions, certificate or soundness theorem (G46). Status gap for certification only.

rules.name: implicit-invocation
rules.derives: Getters, setters, coercion hooks (@@toPrimitive, valueOf, toString), @@hasInstance, destructuring reads, tagged templates, JSX factories and spreads invoke the target set value_targets resolves; an empty closed set contributes nothing, an open set adds a Target unknown and marks receivers escaped.
side_conditions: accessor_targets_of returns the closed empty set whenever the analysed program defines no accessor key at all (value_targets.rs:693-695)
protocol_targets_of returns the closed empty set whenever no program syntax defines one of the keys (value_targets.rs:715-717, 1240-1250)
accessors_on/protocol_targets_within open the set for unresolved receivers only when the key is defined somewhere in the program (value_targets.rs:1524-1526, 1547-1555, 1580-1592)
the key index scans program syntax with bodies only (value_targets.rs:3017-3060, 3408-3423)
declared-primitive operands skip coercion (invocations.rs:1014-1042)
rules.evidence: [S2] The closed sets rest on a closed-world assumption outside §2: that only the analysed program defines accessors or protocol methods on the values a node touches. §2.2 covers only built-in behaviour, and §2.5 admits an input object whose declared property is an accessor. Counterexample: `export function f(o: { x: number }): number { return o.x; }` in a program defining no getter. accessor_keys is empty, so the read is closed and f is Known O(1). An external caller passing `const o = { n: K, get x() { let s = 0; for (let i = 0; i < this.n; i++) s++; return s; } }` conforms to `{ x: number }`, and f's work is Θ(K) with every declared input dimension constant (§3.2). `${o}`, `+o` and `o instanceof C` behave the same way on input values. [S7 tests, compliant] Pinned. The declared-primitive coercion skip rests on axiom 2.5.

rules.name: iterator-visits
rules.derives: An iteration (for-of, spread, yield*, array destructuring) costs acquisition plus count × (next + result getters); the count comes from latent yields, intrinsic iteration sources, native collection sizes, or ONE for a next that returns done:true literally; with no count, the next part is scaled by None and a Bound unknown is retained.
side_conditions: no open acquire/next targets or accessors (invocations.rs:2783-2795)

native iteration with resolved length: an exceeding length is the count; constant- or share-sized is ONE; a length of ONE otherwise falls to count_of(...).unwrap_or(Cost::N) (invocations.rs:2838-2857)
a user next counts ONE only when every returned object literal sets done: true (invocations.rs:2859-2924)
an unknown count keeps the next part once with a Bound unknown and forgets recurrence multiplicity (invocations.rs:752-762)
rules.evidence: [S2] invocations.rs:2854 proves the count Cost::N when the iterable's length is a resolved ONE that is neither constant- nor share-sized and count_of fails. That is the input-size envelope, an assumption outside §2 (§2.1, S2-4 (G5)), and size-substitution then binds it to max(entry roots). unknown_visits_part_of (invocations.rs:408) and rest reads (invocations.rs:1550) scale unknown parts by the same N, which leaks into the printed partial cost. The no-count branch (invocations.rs:752-762) keeps the per-visit cost once in the printed partial cost, departing from §1 Floor (S2-5 (G4)). No certificate (§6.1, §6.4).

rules.name: latent-production
rules.derives: A generator's produced count (yields) is the join over yield sites of the product of enclosing resolved loop factors and delegated counts; a function returning latent values carries a Lazy channel and deferred reading joined over returns; latent_size_of gives consumers a Size whose length is the yields or unresolved.
side_conditions: every enclosing factor is resolved, else the count is None (invocations.rs:871-896)
mixed latent and non-latent returns drop the yields (summaries.rs:4889-4891, 5074-5080)
latent_size_of uses Size::sized(yields or Cost::N) with element Cost::N and marks the length unresolved when yields is None (summaries.rs:5506-5517)
rules.evidence: [S2] Missing from the inventory. The element size stays Cost::N (the envelope) even when the length is resolved, and that feeds S2-2 (G5). No certificate (§6.1, §6.4).

rules.name: lazy-consume
rules.derives: Consuming a latent value (generator object or returned latent) charges its deferred reading at the consumption site (for-of right side, spread, yield*, array destructuring); a latent-returning call whose result is not consumed through a tracked route charges the consumed part at the call with a Multiplicity unknown.
side_conditions: is_tracked_consumption accepts expression statements, conditional tests, non-final sequence items, void, for-of right sides, spreads, delegating yields, value returns, expression-bodied arrows, next/return/throw on unresolved callees, tracked call arguments, const holders whose references are all tracked, and array-pattern destructuring (summaries.rs:5828-5911)
tracking depth at most 6 and LatentStep admission, else untracked (summaries.rs:5834-5836)
a tracked call argument requires closed targets whose parameter is write-free, undefaulted and tracked in turn, or a modelled native that iterates that argument (summaries.rs:5927-5991)
rules.evidence: [S2] Conservative as read: untracked routes add a Multiplicity unknown. The completeness of the tracked-route list is what makes call-lazy-phase's Excluded drop sound, and it is unproven (§6.1, §6.4).

rules.name: returned-function-facts
rules.derives: Callback facts for functions a call returns: each returned expression that is an unwritten parameter carrying a descriptor, or a known callable target, becomes callback facts with captures from the callee's substitutions; async or generator targets and unresolved returns mark the set open.
side_conditions: the callee is neither async nor generator, else open (summaries.rs:4069-4079)
a returned parameter is write-free and holds a descriptor, else open (summaries.rs:4116-4134)
rules.evidence: [S2] Supports the inventory's call-returned-function (walker.rs:2592-2635). No certificate or rule name (§6.1, §6.4, §6.5).

rules.name: size-substitution
rules.derives: A callee cost stated in the callee's parameter names and the legacy envelope N is rewritten into caller terms: each name maps to the argument's size fact, `name.length` aliases the same size for array/string/destructured parameters, and LegacyN binds to max(root sizes), where root sizes are the entry's parameter sizes whenever a root is active.
side_conditions: every referenced name is available, else CostError::UnknownName; an available name without a size fact is CostError::UnresolvedQuantity (summaries.rs:534-549)
a trial bind of every name and root to the placeholder dimension succeeds (summaries.rs:538-541)
roots are the active entry's root sizes when any (summaries.rs:526-528), else the argument sizes, else the placeholder dimension u64::MAX (summaries.rs:530-532)
Cost::bind maps LegacyN to max(roots, ONE) and LegacyLog/LegacyNLog accordingly (cost.rs:675-734)
rules.evidence: [S2] LegacyN is the input-size envelope: binding it to max(entry root sizes) asserts that every untracked size is bounded by the largest entry input, an assumption outside §2 (§2.1). This is the binding point that gives the envelope defaults (values.rs:141-149, values.rs:1015-1029, walker.rs:1389, walker.rs:2729, invocations.rs:2854) their meaning, so a Known bound can undercut the work (§3.2). Counterexamples (verified with the working-tree build): `export function nest(a: number[][]): number { let s = 0; for (const r of a) for (const v of r) s += v; return s; }` reports Known O(max(1, a^2)) while a = [K-element array] does Θ(K) work at |a| = 1; `const store: number[] = []; export function add(x: number) { store[store.length] = x; } export function q(a: number[]) { return [...store].length + a.length; }` reports Known O(a) while q does Θ(K) after K add calls. With no sized inputs the placeholder dimension u64::MAX stands in for 'the input' (summaries.rs:531, 870): `scan()` iterating the same store reports Known O(N). Verified (amended): Verdict stands, but the first counterexample does not reproduce: flatMap's produced size is tracked and `entry` reports O(a^2) (refute-2/p1). Verified replacements: (1) `export function nest(a: number[][]) { for (const r of a) for (const v of r) ... }` is Known O(max(1, a^2)) because the inner length defaults to N (values.rs:141-149 element Cost::N marked resolved) and N binds to |a|; a = [K-element array] does Θ(K) work with |a| = 1 (p5). (2) `const store: number[] = []; export function add(x) { store[store.length] = x; } export function q(a: number[]) { return [...store].length + a.length; }` is Known O(a) while the spread does Θ(K) after K add calls (p4). (3) `scan()` over the same module store with no parameters is Known O(N), N being the placeholder dimension u64::MAX (summaries.rs:530-532, 869-871), which is no input dimension (p1). Checked with the working-tree debug build (target/debug/olint.exe, copied to .scratch/olint-compliance/refute-2/) over refute-2/p1..p5 with --types syntactic --min 0; the working-tree edits touch asserted/snapshot recording, not these paths.

rules.name: target-resolution
rules.derives: The known and open target sets for callees, member dispatch, constructor-context this/super dispatch, class candidates of parameters and heritage, and subclasses; a closed set means the call can reach only the listed functions.
side_conditions: this/super dispatch closes only inside constructors, field initialisers and static blocks (invocations.rs:67-117), and opens when the class is surfaced or its binding escapes other than as a heritage (value_targets.rs:2163-2323)
in-program subclasses join instance dispatch through the lineage index (value_targets.rs:5598-5715, 5079-5130)
a parameter's class candidates close only when every call site of its function is known (value_targets.rs:5522-5570)
member calls resolved through member_of_receiver stay open (types.rs:250-262; receivers.rs:23-154)
resolution depth 24, lineage 32, aliases 8, base classes 32, and exhaustion opens the set (value_targets.rs:34-36, 1052-1063; receivers.rs:12-13)
OUTSIDE_SOURCES_REPLACE_BUILTINS = false encodes §2.2 (value_targets.rs:32, 666)
rules.evidence: [S2] Missing from the inventory, yet every E rule depends on closed target sets. The closure arguments rest on the analysed program being the whole program apart from entry inputs (§1), so they are within the spec as far as this read went, beyond the accessor/protocol index flagged in implicit-invocation. No certificate or rule name (§6.1, §6.4, §6.5).

rules.name: tsc-callee-targets
rules.derives: Known call targets for a static member call from the checker's symbol, aliases, shorthand, initializers, class constructors and resolved signature; always open.
side_conditions: member_of_receiver fails syntactically (types.rs:229-248)
each target maps to an executable declaration in the project, else open (types.rs:418-446)
targets validated as in-bounds UTF-8 spans (types.rs:397-416)
rules.evidence: [S6] No certificate (§6.4). Targets are deduplicated with Vec::contains, Theta(k^2) per site (types.rs:423-433, 250-257, 484-488, S6-7 (G73)). The union-of-n-classes family returns n targets per site (S6-4 (G62)).

rules.name: rec-branching-decrement
rules.derives: A component where some member branches, with every edge a Decrement by the same amount d: factor = (max over members of the summed edge multiplicities)^(measure/d) ('guarded decrement with branching'). Branching of literally 1 is rejected.
side_conditions: uniform decrement amount; multiplicities may be symbolic (loop factors * site counts)
rules.evidence: [S1] The recursion tree has <= sum_k b^k nodes. For symbolic b that may equal 1 this is (depth+1)*b^depth, but Decrement admission requires a constant upper guard, so depth is a program constant and the bound holds up to a constant. Sound. The certificate must use that guard.

rules.name: rec-chain-decrement
rules.derives: A component where every member makes exactly one recursive call (constant multiplicity sum 1), with at least one reducing edge, no Unchanged-only cycle, and some Decrement edge: factor = measure for each member ('guarded decrement depth').
side_conditions: at most 16 members; every edge admissible (rec-guard)
rules.evidence: [S1] Each cycle reduces the measure by >= 1, so calls <= members * (measure - lower + 1) = O(measure). Sound. Gap for §6.1/§6.4/§6.5.

rules.name: rec-chain-division
rules.derives: The same chain shape with only Division reductions: factor = log(measure) ('guarded geometric reduction depth').
side_conditions: as rec-chain-decrement, with no Decrement edge
rules.evidence: [S1] Each cycle divides by >= 2 down to the guard. Sound. log(measure) with a constant measure of 1 yields log(1) = 0 (S1-9 (G49)).

rules.name: rec-factorial
rules.derives: A single-member component with decrement 1 and total multiplicity equal to its measure: factor = measure! ('guarded decrement with measure multiplicity').
side_conditions: exact structural equality of the multiplicity and the measure
rules.evidence: [S1] T(n) = n*T(n-1) has sum_k n!/k! <= e*n! calls. Sound.

rules.name: rec-forget-multiplicity
rules.derives: When an unresolved-bound loop body mentions recurrence dimensions, the recurrence multiplicity is forgotten (the component falls back).
side_conditions: cost mentions a dimension >= RECURRENCE_FLOOR
rules.evidence: [S1] A safety valve that prevents a recurrence factor from being derived under an unknown loop multiplicity. This rule is missing from the inventory.

rules.name: rec-guard
rules.derives: An edge is admissible when its relation shrinks (decrement >= 1 with a lower bound, divisor >= 2) and a division has lower bound >= 0 (truncating) or >= 1 (non-truncating).
side_conditions: lower_bound is the strict lower bound established on the call path
rules.evidence: [S1] Termination conditions are correct for the relation forms admitted. Gap for §6.1/§6.4/§6.5. [S7 tests, compliant] Pinned with negative cases.

rules.name: rec-markers
rules.derives: Recursive-call markers split a member's residue into local cost and a factor on the recurrence dimension (Cost::split_dimension), and build RecurrenceEquations.
side_conditions: split_dimension supports only sums, maxima and single-carrier products of the marker dimension (cost.rs:505-576)
component size at most MAXIMUM_RECURRENCE_MEMBERS and a RecurrenceStep charge (summaries.rs:1980-1984)
shared effects reach a fixpoint within 4 rounds (summaries.rs:1989-2029)
no member evaluation is missing, exhausted or in fallback (summaries.rs:1941-1955)
no unresolved multiplicity touched a marker (summaries.rs:2032-2034, 1832-1836; invocations.rs:755-757)
split_dimension succeeds for every marker, i.e. markers appear only linearly (summaries.rs:6043-6056)
marker parts retain the other members' unknown provenance (summaries.rs:1848-1870)
rules.evidence: [S1] Cross-reference to slice 2 (summaries.rs). The cost.rs part is sound: E <= local + factor*D for the supported shapes, and anything else returns None. [S2] The edge multiplicity is the marker coefficient times the number of recorded call sites (summaries.rs:2155), which over-approximates when sequential composition takes a max. Sites are recorded only on the invocation_reading_of path (summaries.rs:3796-3798); latent_invocation_of's cyclic branch records none (summaries.rs:5395-5404), and edges with zero sites abort the solution (summaries.rs:2145-2153). That makes the sites premise plausible but unproven (S2-15 (G55)). No certificate (§6.1, §6.4). [S7 tests, compliant] Pinned in unit tests.

rules.name: rec-measure
rules.derives: A member's measure is the substituted value size of its `number`-annotated parameter in the recurrence slot.
side_conditions: TS annotation `number` on an identifier parameter (§2.5)
substitution present in the task inputs
slot candidates start from member 0's parameter positions and propagate along steps; any inconsistency rejects the candidate (summaries.rs:2180-2201, 6113-6165)
every site of an edge admits the measure: non-measure arguments preserved, no spread (summaries.rs:6066-6078; recurrences.rs:34-48, 531-585)
the measure is the size fact of a numeric parameter binding (recurrences.rs:430-440)
relations fold with weaker_relation_of and lower bounds with f64::min (summaries.rs:6080-6111)
rules.evidence: [S1] Relies on §2.5 and on the value-size quantity of a number, which the Lean model must define (S1-9 (G49)/S1-11 (G50)). Gap for §6.1/§6.4/§6.5. [S2] The slot search and folds do not depend on HashMap order: every order yields the same result or the same rejection. Lower bounds are f64, which a Lean certificate needs as exact rationals (§6.3, S2-14 (G57)). No certificate (§6.1, §6.4).

rules.name: rec-reduced-measure-size
rules.derives: The size of a reduced recursive argument (x - a, x / d, ...) is the substituted size of its unwritten source parameter.
side_conditions: relation is not Unchanged; source is an unwritten parameter
rules.evidence: [S1] For a decrement of a negative value the magnitude grows by a constant, which stays within O(size). It is otherwise an over-approximation. This rule is missing from the inventory.

rules.name: rec-relation
rules.derives: Per call argument: Unchanged (identifier), Decrement{a} (x - a or x + (-a), with integer a in [1, 2^53]), Division{d, truncating} (x / d, x >> k, Math.floor/trunc, | 0 of a division, with integer d in [2, 2^32]). Kept only when the source parameter is unwritten and the path guards admit the relation, or when a shift/|0 coerces.
side_conditions: numeric_guards_of: enclosing if/conditional/logical tests and preceding unconditionally-exiting ifs in enclosing blocks; lower bounds strict, upper inclusive
Decrement needs finiteness (ordered or Number.isFinite) and both lower >= -2^53 and upper <= 2^53; Division needs finiteness
argument_bounds_of: other arguments preserved or shrinking
rules.evidence: [S1] NaN handling is correct: negated comparisons are unordered, so they give no finiteness. Requiring an upper guard for Decrement bounds the recursion depth by a program constant. Soundness uses double semantics (x - 1 == x above 2^53; ToInt32 for the coercing forms), so S1-11 (G50) applies. [S7 tests, compliant] Pinned; the depth-cap degradation is a 7.4 concern (S7-5 (G67)).

rules.name: rec-relation-join
rules.derives: Several call sites from caller to callee combine their relations with weaker_relation_of: any Unchanged makes it Unchanged, the smaller decrement, Decrement over Division, the smaller divisor. Lower bounds combine by min.
side_conditions: every site has a step for the (caller, callee) slot pair, else no relation
rules.evidence: [S1] Treating Decrement{a} with Division{d} as Decrement{a} overstates per-step reduction only while x < a*d/(d-1), a constant region, so depth stays O(measure/a). Sound asymptotically. This rule is missing from the inventory.

rules.name: rec-unsolved
rules.derives: Components without a solution (Unsupported reasons in solution_of) fall back to unknown recursion handling in summaries.
side_conditions: SCC detection over waiting tasks with every outside dependency Ready (summaries.rs:1517-1628)
fallback readings for every member computed first (summaries.rs:1704-1719)
RecurrenceContext at most 4096 admissions and QueuePush charges, else the fallback record (summaries.rs:2247-2253, 2268-2271, 2290-2297)
published effects join Effects::unknown() with the members' effects (summaries.rs:1768-1776)
rules.evidence: [S1] Cross-reference to slice 2. The recurrences.rs side only returns Unsupported reasons. [S2] Derives Partial or Unknown only: every recursive re-entry carries an unknown, and local_resource_reading retains a ResourceExhaustion unknown (the unknown joins part.unknowns, cost.rs:1699-1704). No certificate for the proven contributions in the floor (§6.4, §6.5). Context enumeration is exponential in component size up to the fixed cap (S2-10 (G69)).

rules.name: array-method
rules.derives: An Array/TypedArray-kind receiver calling an ARRAY_LINEAR method is charged its produced length (else N) times the callback; ARRAY_N_LOG_N (sort, toSorted) is charged length*log(length) times the comparator; constant-sized or share-sized receivers charge the callback once.
side_conditions: the method's steps loop at most len times with O(1) work per iteration beyond the callback
sort performs O(n log n) comparisons
no user code beyond the callback runs (species, element ToString, argument coercion)
rules.evidence: [S4] sort/toSorted (tables.rs:35, walker.rs:2713, 2728-2731) are charged N log N but 23.1.3.30.1 SortIndexedProperties sorts 'using an implementation-defined sequence of calls to SortCompare' (same for %TypedArray%.prototype.sort 23.2.3.29 and toSorted 23.1.3.34/23.2.3.33); §2.4 requires unknown. join (23.1.3.18) is charged receiver length but its output is sum of element-string lengths plus (n-1)*|sep| and it calls ToString on each element. map/filter/slice/splice/flat/flatMap call ArraySpeciesCreate (10.4.2.3) whose constructor/@@species may be user code; only concat handles species (native.rs:2001-2105). Numeric argument coercions (fromIndex, start, end, index, target) invoke ToIntegerOrInfinity (user valueOf) and are not charged in this branch. See S4-1 (G8), S4-11 (G12), S4-12 (G13), S4-13 (G14), S4-14 (G52). [S7 tests, compliant] Pinned, but sort is asserted n log n against 2.3/2.4 (S7-1 (G8)). String-method constants (literal receiver) are not checked against ES steps.

rules.name: intrinsic-replacement-scan
rules.derives: Whether the analysed program replaces or extends a built-in member, accessor or prototype, from a whole-program scan of writes, defineProperty/assign reflective writes and prototype reassignments; unreplaced built-ins keep their native models.
side_conditions: outside sources never replace built-ins (value_targets.rs:32), which is §2.2
replacement queries answer from the collected write index (value_targets.rs:2524-2623, 2864-2896, 6515-6745)
rules.evidence: [S2] Encodes §2.2 directly, so it is within §2. Missing from the inventory. No certificate (§6.1, §6.4).

rules.name: linear-constructor
rules.derives: An unresolved, non-MODELS `new C(x)` with C named in LINEAR_CONSTRUCTORS is charged Cost::N when x is neither constant-sized, a numeric constant nor share-sized, else O(1), with no unknown.
side_conditions: C is the intrinsic constructor
the constructor's steps are O(size of x) with no user code
a numeric length argument's magnitude is bounded by N
rules.evidence: [S4] At HEAD walker.rs:2064-2105 the LINEAR_CONSTRUCTORS fallback matches the bare identifier name without is_intrinsic_reference. It is reached only when construction targets are unresolved and construction_model_of returned None (a non-intrinsic binding, or an intrinsic without a model). It returns Cost::N, or nothing for constant arguments, with no unknown and no intrinsic_replaced_of check. The binary confirms that a parameter named Map yields Known O(N). WeakSet/WeakMap (24.4.1.1, 24.3.1.1) iterate their argument through the iterator protocol (user next(), and generators of any length) and call the adder per element, and neither is charged. ArrayBuffer/SharedArrayBuffer (25.1.4.1 CreateByteDataBlock zero-fills `length` bytes) and TypedArray(length) do work proportional to the numeric value, which Cost::N bounds only if numeric magnitudes are input dimensions. See S4-21 (G18). Verified (amended): Unsoundness confirmed with the binary: export function f(Map: MapConstructor, xs) { return new Map(xs) } reports 'calls Map(xs) = O(N)' as Known with no unknown, while the same code with a parameter named C draws 'unknown call target'. new WeakSet(xs: Iterable<object>) is Known O(xs) with no iterator-protocol charge. Correction: nothing drops an open remainder here. open_remainder_of (HEAD walker.rs:1923-1939) returns None whenever targets are unresolved, and the fallback is reached only after 'if resolved { return }' at walker.rs:2046. The defect is that the fallback returns without an unknown. Omission: the fallback also serves intrinsic constructors that have no model (Array, WeakSet, WeakMap, ArrayBuffer, SharedArrayBuffer, DataView), and it skips the intrinsic_replaced_of check that the model path makes at walker.rs:2053, so an unknown-key globalThis write adds no unknown there. [S7 tests, compliant] Pinned (Set, Uint8Array); see S7-2 (G6).

rules.name: native-callback
rules.derives: A Callback(Count) role invokes the argument's resolved targets Once (beside) or PerElement/PerMatch/PerVisit (inner, multiplied by the charge); PerMatch collapses to Once for non-global literal or primitive patterns.
side_conditions: the steps invoke the callback at most once per charged unit
the callback cannot enlarge the traversal the charge measures
Count::PerMatch -> Once only when the pattern cannot match twice (22.2.6.11 non-global exec runs once; string pattern replaces the first occurrence, 22.1.3.19)
rules.evidence: [S4] JSON.parse reviver is Callback(PerElement) over the text length (native.rs:272-277), but 25.5.1.1 InternalizeJSONProperty reads Get(holder, name) after the reviver ran on earlier siblings, so a reviver that writes holder[sibling] = largeOrCyclic makes the walk unbounded by the text.
