Other counts (array iteration methods use the initial len, 23.1.3.x; PerMatch rule for replace) agree with the steps. See S4-18 (G17). [S7 tests, compliant] Pinned; the sort comparator case (O(N^2 log N)) rests on the S7-1 (G8) model.

rules.name: native-charge-length
rules.derives: The multiplicity charged for a modelled built-in is the size of one measured operand (receiver, first argument, keys, elements, output or visit budget), else N; constant-sized or share-sized operands charge O(1).
side_conditions: the measured operand's size bounds every loop in the steps
no other operand (needle, replacement, separator, other set, fill string, element strings) contributes a superconstant factor
numeric-magnitude operands (lengths, counts) are bounded by the measured size
rules.evidence: [S4] Work::Linear(Operand::Receiver) for includes/indexOf/lastIndexOf/split/replaceAll (native.rs:395-456) charges Cost::N, which reports as the max of the call's dimensions (e.g. O(max(s,t)) for s.includes(t), checked with the binary). is_native_bounded (native.rs:1352-1386) never inspects the needle/separator/replacement, and matching_part_of returns Part::none() for primitive patterns (regex.rs:810). ECMA-262 6.1.4.1 StringIndexOf is O((n-m+1)*m), Theta(s*t) at t = s/2; 22.1.3.11 lastIndexOf likewise. GetSubstitution runs per match, O(k*|replacement|) for replaceAll and global replace. localeCompare is implementation-defined (S4-2 (G9)). See S4-9 (G10), S4-10 (G11). Verified (amended): The verdict holds but the evidence overstated it. Cost::N resolves to the max over the call's dimensions: s.includes(t) reports O(max(t, s)) and s.replaceAll('a', r) O(max(s, r)). So the needle and replacement sizes enter additively, and what goes uncharged is their product with the receiver or with the match count. Single-match replace with a string pattern, O(n + r), is covered by the max.

rules.name: native-model
rules.derives: A call or construction resolved to an intrinsic with a MODELS entry gets the entry's Work (Constant or Linear over one Operand), its argument Roles (callbacks, coercions, patterns, iterated operands) and its Output size, composed by native_reading_of.
side_conditions: callee is an intrinsic reference (is_intrinsic_reference) or a receiver of the declared Kind
the entry's Work is at least the worst-case work of the ECMA-262 steps of that built-in (§2.3)
the built-in's work is fully specified by ECMA-262 steps (§2.4), and the built-in is an ECMA-262 built-in at all
every user code the steps may invoke (coercion, getters, species, protocol methods) is charged through a Role
rules.evidence: [S4] Entries violate §2.4 (localeCompare, toLocaleLowerCase, toLocaleUpperCase in STRING_LINEAR modelled Linear(Receiver) at native.rs:450-456 via tables.rs:69-98; ECMA-262 22.1.3.12/.26/.27 make the work implementation-defined/locale-dependent), rest on no ECMA-262 steps at all (Buffer.from/concat/alloc/allocUnsafe/compare native.rs:290-320 and structuredClone native.rs:321-327 are host APIs), and undercut §2.3 (Set.add, Map.set, Set/Map delete/clear Work::Constant at native.rs:457-496 while 24.1.3.1/.3/.9 and 24.2.4.1/.2/.4 scan [[MapData]]/[[SetData]] with explicit For-each loops; string search entries charge only the receiver while StringIndexOf 6.1.4.1 is O(n*m); JSON.stringify Graph charge ignores indentation output Theta(N*depth)). See gaps S4-1 (G8)..S4-5 (G6), S4-9 (G10), S4-10 (G11), S4-16 (G7)..S4-20 (G39). [S7 tests, compliant] Costs of individual natives are pinned by exact-O assertions, but only against the model, never against ECMAScript worst-case steps; see S7-1 (G8) and S7-2 (G6) for models the spec contradicts. No test asserts that an implementation-defined native yields an unknown contribution (2.4).

rules.name: native-visit-budget
rules.derives: For PerVisit callbacks (Set/Map forEach) and iterated constructors with callbacks/adders, the charge is the live visit budget computed from the callback bodies' writes to the traversed collection (live_visits_of), else Unresolved.
side_conditions: Map/Set forEach re-reads numEntries after each callback (24.1.3.5, 24.2.4.7) so growth during iteration is included
the traversed List length equals the live collection size
rules.evidence: [S4] Growth during forEach is handled via live_visits_of. The second side condition fails under the literal steps: delete (24.1.3.3) and clear (24.1.3.1) replace entries by ~empty~ without removing them, so forEach/iteration walks every entry ever added since construction; the charged live size undercuts that. Depends on the S4-5 (G6)/S4-6 (G36) decision. No certificate.

rules.name: regex-cost
rules.derives: A literal regex (or a string literal compiled by match/matchAll/search) is classified by the recheck 4.5.0 automaton checker in a Node sidecar; Constant/Linear/Polynomial(d<=16) becomes subject^d nested at the call; Safe, Exponential, unsupported, dynamic patterns become unknown; timeout/cancel become ResourceExhaustion.
side_conditions: recheck's degree bounds the ECMA-262 22.2.2 Pattern-semantics step count of one RegExpBuiltinExec (22.2.7.2), including the lastIndex scan over start positions
the bound holds for exec from any lastIndex (g/y flags) including patterns with lookbehind/\b/^
recheck's answer is a premise the axioms (§2) admit
classification is deterministic (§3.4)
rules.evidence: [S4] The degree comes from an external heuristic oracle (recheck's prioritised-NFA ambiguity analysis), not from ECMA-262 steps; §2.1 lets proven results rest only on signed axioms and §6.1 needs a proof-record theorem, so a Known bound resting on recheck is unsupported. Unverified premises: that recheck's degree includes the RegExpBuiltinExec step-13 scan (the /\s+$/ quadratic class suggests it does) and counts the same steps as 22.2.2 (RepeatMatcher empty-check, capture-list copies, Canonicalize under i/u/v); Matching::Once is applied to RegExp test/exec (walker.rs:2799-2803) even with g/y where exec starts at a nonzero lastIndex and lookbehind/\b see the prefix, while is_context_free guards only the Repeated path. Sidecar timeouts are wall-clock (regex.rs:69-70, 10 s/120 s), so Exhausted vs Bound depends on the machine, contrary to §3.4. Backreferences/unsupported features correctly become unknown. See S4-22 (G20, G47), S4-23 (G29), S4-24 (G19). [S7 tests, compliant] Pinned via exact cost assertions; helper exhaustion cases depend on wall-clock timeouts (S7-3 (G29)).

rules.name: regex-every-match
rules.derives: For Repeated matching (global flag, matchAll, replaceAll, split) of a context-free classified pattern (no ^, \b, \B, lookbehind), cost = subject * recheck cost; non-context-free repeated patterns add an UnsupportedModel unknown.
side_conditions: each exec starting at lastIndex k costs at most the classified bound, which holds when the pattern cannot observe the prefix
at most subject+1 execs (AdvanceStringIndex on empty matches, 22.2.6.8/.11; sticky attempts per q in 22.2.6.14)
rules.evidence: [S4] The derivation is sound relative to the regex-cost premise: for context-free patterns an attempt at k equals a from-0 attempt on the suffix, execs advance lastIndex by at least 1, and @@split's sticky attempts are each bounded by the suffix search. Inherits the regex-cost premise (S4-22 (G20, G47)). No certificate.

rules.name: regex-matched-once
rules.derives: A pattern starting with ^, without the m flag and without top-level alternation matches at most at index 0, so global/Repeated matching is priced as one match and per-match callbacks as Once.
side_conditions: ^ without m asserts position 0 (22.2.2.6 Assertion ^: e = 0 when Multiline is false)
no top-level | lets another alternative match elsewhere
class and escape scanning of the source text is correct for u/v flags
rules.evidence: [S4] Sound under 22.2.2.6 and 22.2.6.11/.14: after a match at 0 the next exec (global) or sticky split attempt at q>0 fails ^ in O(1) per position, so at most one result and one callback; the residual O(n) failed scan is covered by the Linear(Receiver) charge. Scanner handles escapes, nested v-mode classes and [] / [^]. Quantified ^ is a SyntaxError, so no bypass. No certificate (§6.1).

rules.name: set-map-linear
rules.derives: A Set-kind receiver calling union/intersection/difference/symmetricDifference/isSubsetOf/isSupersetOf/isDisjointFrom (and the shadowed Set/Map forEach) is charged Cost::N with no argument contributions.
side_conditions: work bounded by N independent of the other operand
the other operand is a native Set with intrinsic size/has/keys
rules.evidence: [S4] ES2025 Set methods (24.2.4.5 difference, .9 intersection, .10 isDisjointFrom, .11 isSubsetOf, .12 isSupersetOf, .15 symmetricDifference, .16 union) call GetSetRecord(other) (24.2.1.2) which reads user-definable size/has/keys, iterate other.keys() (O(|other|)) or call other.has per element, and dedupe with SetDataHas, a List scan (O(|result|) per step). walker.rs:2770-2786 charges a flat Cost::N and invokes nothing for the argument. forEach entries in SET_LINEAR/MAP_LINEAR are shadowed by MODELS (native.rs:497-510). See S4-15 (G15), S4-28 (G86). [S7 tests, compliant] Pinned linear; contradicts 2.3 per ES list-scan steps (S7-2 (G6)). No test pins Set/Map has/get/add/set/delete cost.

rules.name: unmodelled-native
rules.derives: A call whose native is not modelled, or whose receiver Kind is Unknown, or whose Receiver-kind method has no table entry, is an unknown contribution (UnsupportedModel or Target).
side_conditions: every unmodelled intrinsic call yields an unknown contribution (§2.4 direction is safe)
is_modelled agrees with what intrinsic_reading_of can price
rules.evidence: [S4] Unknown is the §2.4-safe outcome, so Map.get/has, Set.has, Array push/pop/at, String at/charAt fall to UnsupportedModel soundly (they are specified linear scans or O(1) and could be modelled). is_modelled (walker.rs:2835-2844) returns true for Receiver(Array|Set|Map|String|RegExp) even when the method will fall to UnsupportedModel, and false for Native::Unmodelled; at walker.rs:2555-2565 an intrinsic-replaced call with known user targets adds the intrinsic alternative only when is_modelled, so an Unmodelled intrinsic alternative contributes nothing there unless open_remainder_of (walker.rs:2524) already charged it. Needs refutation check. See S4-7 (G6, G45), S4-8. [S7 tests, compliant] Pinned for methods absent from the tables. No test enumerates implementation-defined built-ins (sort, etc.) as unmodelled, so coverage stops short of 2.4.

rules.name: argument-facts
rules.derives: Per-argument facts at a call: size (integer literal value max 1, `p.length` of a string/array parameter, produced size, reduced measure size), aliasing to unwritten parameters through const initialisers, callback descriptors, latent records, definedness, parameter defaults when the argument is undefined, and a rest parameter sized ONE when every collected argument is constant-sized.
side_conditions: integer literal in [0, 2^53-1] with zero fraction (summaries.rs:2911-2919)
`.length` aliasing requires the declared type kind String or Array and a substitution for the binding (summaries.rs:2968-2989)
parameter aliasing requires is_parameter_unwritten (write-free, no dynamic scope) (summaries.rs:2955-2966, 3979-3990)
rest ONE requires no spread before the rest position and constant-sized spreads (summaries.rs:3915-3977)
a failed latent record sets the exhausted flag (summaries.rs:3032-3038)
rules.evidence: [S2] The inventory places argument-facts at summaries.rs:2787-3060. Size facts rest on §2.5 for `.length` of declared arrays and strings, which is inside §2. No certificate (§6.1, §6.4).

rules.name: array-method-size
rules.derives: Result size of Array methods: map via result-size, toSpliced as source plus inserted arguments, and filter, slice, sort, toSorted, reverse, toReversed, fill, copyWithin, with, splice as the source size.

The callee member is intrinsic (types.rs and native.rs call site).
rules.evidence: [S3] Every listed method returns at most the receiver's length (splice returns the removed elements) or adds counted items, so the size is an upper bound. The receiver kind comes from declared-kind (see S3-3 (G21), S3-10 (G27)).

rules.name: constant-cardinality
rules.derives: An expression has size Cost::ONE (Cardinality::Constant) when its measure is constant and, for Length use, its shape is linear (primitive, fixed typed array or array); for Keys use, constant keys; for Enumerated use, constant keys with no extendable inherited keys.
side_conditions: Literal arrays and objects: every spread argument is itself constant-sized (value_sizes.rs:417-441); object properties are plain init data properties with inert values and no __proto__ key.
String concatenation with a constant primitive operand and a numeric-constant other operand (value_sizes.rs:458-472).
`new Array(k)` or typed array with one numeric-constant argument and no replaced intrinsic (value_sizes.rs:514-536).

Derived method calls (map, filter, slice, concat, sort, toSorted, reverse, toReversed, with, toSpliced, flatMap) on a constant receiver, an intrinsic member, and constant-sized concat arguments or a constant-returning flatMap callback (value_sizes.rs:538-622).
Object.keys/values/entries/assign/freeze of constant-key arguments with the intrinsic member unreplaced.
Variables: const with initializer, holder stability where the shape needs history (value_sizes.rs:624-655).
rules.evidence: [S3] No unsound path found. Non-addition binary and unary expressions are non-constant, non-const variables and parameters are VARIABLE, enum, object and array literals are checked structurally, and unresolved depth returns VARIABLE (value_sizes.rs:411-413). It depends on is_intrinsic_member, which uses the program-wide member-name dispatch (value_targets.rs:609-683) whose OUTSIDE_SOURCES_REPLACE_BUILTINS=false constant (value_targets.rs:32) is an assumption outside §2 (slice 2 owns it). The rule names no proof rule, records no side conditions and has no certificate (§6.1, §6.4, §6.5). is_numeric_constant also folds readonly class members, see known-value-declaration. [S7 tests, compliant] Pinned with many negative cases.

rules.name: count-of
rules.derives: The numeric count of an expression: ONE for a numeric constant, the parameter size for a parameter, else the length of a resolved collection size.
side_conditions: For `x.length`, length_resolved holds (Size::sized sets it true for envelope defaults).
rules.evidence: [S3] Depends on is_numeric_constant (readonly-member fold, see known-value-declaration) and on the input-size-envelope default for `x.length` of an underived collection (counted length_resolved=true, so no unknown is reported).

rules.name: growth-sites
rules.derives: The size of an unstable local array holder is its initial size combined with, per push or unshift call in its own function, the pushed arguments' sizes repeated by the enclosing loops' visit counts. Any non-local, written or unclassified use opens the length (length_resolved=false).
side_conditions: The holder is a local variable inside a function, and the file has no direct eval (value_sizes.rs:720-783).
Each growing call is an intrinsic push or unshift local to the holder's function.
Loop factors come from bound_of; a loop with no factor makes the visits None and the length unresolved (values.rs:1183-1223).
for-of loops multiply by the produced size when it exceeds, else by the loop factor.
rules.evidence: [S3] Opening the length on any unclassified use reports an unknown SizeRelation contribution in the consumers (walker.rs:1400-1411), which is sound direction. The loop factor is taken from the loop bound of the enclosing loop only, not from calls that re-enter the function, which is fine because the holder is local. The module-level (function.is_none) case returns Unstable and falls to the input-size-envelope default, see that rule. No named rule or certificate.

rules.name: holder-stability
rules.derives: A variable holding an array, typed array, string or object is stable when no reference can grow, shrink or replace it, so a constant measure at initialisation holds at every use.
side_conditions: No direct eval in the file (value_sizes.rs:813-823, 867-869).
The variable is not exported, ambient, or a script-scope global (value_sizes.rs:889-909).

Every value reference passes is_stable_use: allowed contexts are comparisons, conditions, reading calls (Object.keys and similar, Array.isArray, Array.from), for-of and for-in heads, alias declarations that are themselves stable, spread and template use with inert built-in members, isolated callbacks (at most 2 or 3 parameters, no rest, no dynamic scope), and shrink-only pop, shift and splice with at most two non-spread arguments for a non-exact holder.
A returned holder must be local to its declaring function and that function must exist (value_sizes.rs:825-835).
Alias chains stop at depth 8 (value_sizes.rs:24, 857-861).
rules.evidence: [S3] The check errs conservative: unknown parent kinds return false, argument passing to user calls is unstable, index and property writes are unstable. No counterexample found. The reads depend on builtin_members_replaced, builtin_accessors_defined and is_intrinsic_member, which key on program-wide names (assumption OUTSIDE_SOURCES_REPLACE_BUILTINS=false). No named rule, side-condition record or certificate.

rules.name: input-size-envelope
rules.derives: A collection, iterable or count whose size no rule derives has length N and element size N (or ONE for declared-primitive elements). Loops over it, x.length counts and sorts are charged Cost::N. Sizes built from it carry exceeds=false and length_resolved=true, so no unknown contribution is reported.
side_conditions: None established. The default applies to every collection expression that is not constant-sized, not an unwritten parameter with a substituted size, and not produced by a modelled operation.
Size::sized fixes element = Cost::N (values.rs:145); Size::unresolved and Size::flattened reuse it (values.rs:153, 183).
input_size_of substitutes Cost::N when parameter_size_of fails (values.rs:1018-1022).
rules.evidence: [S3] Cost::N is Expression::LegacyN (cost.rs:265), not a dimension of an entry. Spec §1 defines cost over input dimensions (size quantities of values that enter an entry or a module's evaluation) and §2.1 admits no axiom that every other collection is O(N). Counterexample 1 (state that is not an input): `const buf: number[] = []; export function fill(a: number[]) { for (const x of a) for (const y of a) buf.push(x * y); } export function drain() { for (const v of buf) {} }`. holder_size_of finds an unstable holder (module level, push outside the reading set), holder_growth_of returns Unstable, produced_size_at returns None, input_size_of returns length N (values.rs:1015-1029), and bounds.rs:322-324 charges the loop O(N). After fill(a) with |a|=n, buf holds n^2 elements and drain does n^2 work, and drain has no input dimension. Counterexample 2 (a computed size): `export function f(n: number) { const a = grow(n); for (const v of a) {} } function grow(n: number) { const r = [0]; for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) r.push(...r); return r; }`. call_size_of returns None for a non-native callee (native.rs:3259-3289), so `a` gets length N; the loop does 2^n iterations and n is a number, not a size dimension. Both defeat §3.2 (a Known cost is a bound in every instance) and §4.1 (Within). The report envelope substitution N (report.rs:134) is presentation only. Verified (amended): Verdict upheld; locations extended. Both counterexamples trace at HEAD: CE1 buf is module level, so growth_summary_of returns Unstable (value_sizes.rs:727-731), holder_size_of returns None (values.rs:1135), collection_size_at falls to input_size_of length N (values.rs:1015-1029), iteration_count_at returns N (invocations.rs:2838-2856); no effects.rs guard applies because drain's loop neither writes nor calls unknown code (loop_invalidation_of, effects.rs:808-866). CE2 grow is a user callee, native_of returns Unmodelled (native.rs:681-688), call_size_of gives None, local `a` is Stable so produced stays None and the loop is charged N. Added envelope entry points the slice missed: count_of(...).unwrap_or(Cost::N) in iteration_count_at (invocations.rs:2854), the visit-budget max with Cost::N (bounds.rs:300), linear_bound_of factor Cost::N (bounds.rs:2247, used for for-in over open objects and loops without a derivable body), and Size::sized(latent.yields.unwrap_or(Cost::N)) (summaries.rs:5510).

rules.name: parameter-size
rules.derives: An unwritten parameter identifier has the size cost its call substitution carries: the entry parameter's size dimension, or the argument's size at an inner call.
side_conditions: The expression is a bare identifier resolving to a parameter binding with a single identifier pattern (types.rs:62-80).
is_parameter_unwritten holds for the binding.
current_substitutions has facts for the binding with size Some.

rules.name: produced-size
rules.derives: The Size (length, element, exceeds, resolved flags) of an array literal, conditional, `new` of a modelled constructor, native call result, or holder variable.
side_conditions: Depth at most 16 and SizeStep work budget available; else Size::unresolved (values.rs:1037-1039).

Identifier: const Variable with initializer, size composed with growth sites.

The exceeds flag decides whether a loop uses the computed length or the envelope N (walker.rs:1393-1400), so a wrong exceeds=false on a size derived from a computation would under-charge. rules.name: rest-copy

rules.name: result-size
rules.derives: The element size of `map` results from the callback's returned expressions: a returned first parameter yields the source element, primitive operands yield a constant, other expressions their collection size, joined over all known targets. side_conditions: Callback targets closed and known (targets.open false).

Depth at most 16.

rules.name: size-algebra
rules.derives: combined (max of lengths and elements, or of flags), producing and flattened (length times element, flagged exceeds), repeated (length times count), containing (element := result length), and the size_sum_of/size_product_of primitives.
side_conditions: Constants (constant_of) are dropped from sums and collapse to ONE in products.
Any CostError (resource) collapses to Size::unresolved.
Sum is max: valid asymptotically for sizes.
rules.evidence: [S3] The algebra over-approximates: a sum is bounded by twice its max, a product is exact. `terms.dedup()` removes only adjacent equal terms (values.rs:114), which is safe (max is idempotent). Unresolved flags propagate by conjunction. The proof rules are not named and the family has no certificate. Cost::maximum and multiply belong to family A.

rules.name: size-dimension
rules.derives: One Domain::Size dimension per (value, quantity), with the labels the report prints.

The quantity is Length, Keys or Value.

No proof rule or certificate.

answer recorded in a Recording pass (types.rs:373-391)

rules.derives: A function carrying `@perf O(...)` has its body replaced by the directive cost bound into the specialisation's substitutions (summaries-side half of the inventory's dir-cost); raw summaries skip the directive for the report's raw pass.
side_conditions: bind_known binds the directive cost; Resource/Overflow gives a ResourceExhaustion unknown, other errors raise a diagnostic and an UnsupportedModel unknown (summaries.rs:2390-2417)

not for cyclic calls

parts holding no work are marked Absent

some analysis budget or structural cap rejected a charge or was reached
