rules.evidence: [S2] Sound, since it only lowers nodes. It breaks §7.4: the budget is global and fixed, so a node falls to Unknown once enough unrelated program has spent the budget, with no scaling family showing its own proof's counts growing (§7.4, §7.2; S2-7 (G67)). Which node exhausts depends on evaluation order, which follows RandomState hash iteration (§3.4; S2-6 (G30)). finish_reading also tags bind failures with this reason (S2-13 (G35)). [S6] §7.4 lets a node fall to Unknown under §7 only where a scaling family shows its proof counts growing faster than constant per node, with every other result standing. The limits behind this rule are mostly program-global per-pass totals (see the resource-* rules), so a node's state depends on the size of unrelated code and on scheduling order; the unknown is not attributed to the node whose work grew (§7.2). [S7 tests, compliant] Pinned; the rule itself (cap exhaustion lowers node state) is the subject of S7-5 (G67).

rules.name: resource-flow-limit
rules.derives: ResourceExhaustion when a function's control-flow build exceeds 20,000 units.
side_conditions: FlowContext::build_with_limit returns FlowError::ResourceLimit
rules.evidence: [S6] Per-function constant cap; a function larger than the cap is Unknown with no scaling-family evidence (§7.4, S6-26 (G82)).

rules.name: resource-implementation-files
rules.derives: Runtime implementation files beyond 4096 are not loaded; implementation_stats.exhausted is set and their targets stay unresolved.
side_conditions: stats.files >= IMPLEMENTATION_FILE_LIMIT
rules.evidence: [S6] Program-global count; whether a given import resolves depends on how many other implementation files were visited first (S6-12 (G67)).

rules.name: resource-public-surface
rules.derives: ResourceExhaustion issue on public-surface discovery when the shared 100,000-step counter runs out, or a class lineage reaches 256 or cycles.
side_conditions: Walk.remaining == 0 (shared across all entrypoints and the CommonJS walk)
lineage.len() == 256 or revisited class
rules.evidence: [S6] The 100,000 counter is program-global; with visited reset per entrypoint (public_surface.rs:104-107) the counter is drained by E entrypoints each re-walking the shared graph, so coverage of later entries depends on entrypoint count (S6-21 (G75)).

rules.name: resource-regex-limits
rules.derives: RegexAnswer::Exhausted (ResourceExhaustion) for a pattern over 4096 bytes, beyond the 1024th pattern in a batch, after the 120 s batch deadline, on recheck timeout/cancel, on helper failure, or on an oversized reply.
side_conditions: RegexLimits reached (regex.rs:56-77)
rules.evidence: [S6] Timeout and deadline are wall-clock (§3.4, S6-23 (G29)); the 1024-pattern cap is per batch across the program, so the 1025th distinct pattern is Unknown regardless of its own cost (§7.4, S6-12 (G67)).

rules.name: resource-scheduler-budget
rules.derives: ResourceExhaustion when the per-pass WorkBudget rejects a charge (uniform 4,000,000 per event; TaskKey 20,000; BodyPass 100,000; CallbackDescriptor 20,000; RecurrenceContext 4096; CaptureEdge 200,000), falling back to reserved fallback credit where a task was admitted.
side_conditions: WorkBudget::check fails for some event (analysis_work.rs:193-211)
task not already Ready
rules.evidence: [S6] The budget is one per analysis pass over all selected functions (Scheduler::new in reset_between_passes), not per node. Family: n independent `export function f_i(){ return i }`; past n = 20,000 TaskKey rejects and later functions become Unknown although each needs constant work (S6-12 (G67)).

rules.name: resource-specialization-cap
rules.derives: ResourceExhaustion for a call whose target already has 32 specializations for the same (function, raw, root_sizes).
side_conditions: function_counts[(function, raw, root_sizes)] >= 32 or fallback active
rules.evidence: [S6] Per-function constant cap, compatible with §7.1, but no scaling family in the evaluation corpus justifies it (§7.4), and which 32 specializations win depends on HashSet-driven evaluation order (S6-22 (G30)).

rules.name: resource-trace-arena
rules.derives: ResourceExhaustion (CostError::Resource) when the explanation arena exceeds 1,000,000 nodes, 2,000,000 edges, 64 children per node, 4096 label bytes per node or 64 MiB of labels in total.
side_conditions: TraceArena admission fails
rules.evidence: [S6] Program-global and never cleared between recording passes (reset_between_passes leaves traces untouched), so a node's explanation can fail because of other nodes' traces; interning (TraceArena.interned) absorbs identical re-walks, so only traces that changed in earlier rounds add pressure (S6-12 (G67), S6-15 (G80)). Verified (amended): Program-global and never cleared (Analysis::new only) is correct, but TraceArena interns records by TraceKey, so re-walking unchanged functions in later rounds hits the intern table rather than growing the arena; only traces that change between rounds (after new tsc/regex answers) accumulate. The cross-node dependence claim stands; the 'earlier rounds' part is weaker than stated.

rules.name: tsc-candidate-cap
rules.derives: Callee candidate expansion stops after 1024 symbols; the answer is always open:true.
side_conditions: seen.size >= MAXIMUM_CANDIDATE_SYMBOLS
rules.evidence: [S6] Constant per-query cap; the answer is always open, so truncation cannot close a target set (types.rs:418-446 keeps open). Per-query work is still not constant because each symbol's declarations and class members are scanned (S6-4 (G62)).

rules.name: definedness
rules.derives: Whether an expression is definitely undefined, definitely not undefined, or unknown, used for default-parameter and undefined-argument reasoning.
side_conditions: Depth below 8.
Parameters only when unwritten and carried in current_substitutions.
Literals, operators, `new`, object, array, function and class expressions are Defined; `void` and an undeclared `undefined` are Undefined.
Logical and conditional joins follow truthiness from known values; const initializers and readonly members are followed through stable_initializer_of.
Falls back to known_value_at.
rules.evidence: [S3] The case analysis is correct for the ECMAScript semantics (`a && b`, `a || b`, `a ?? b` joins checked). Unknown wins on any doubt. Consumers: summaries.rs:2824, 3882, 4044, value_targets.rs:4087, walker.rs:188. Inherits the readonly-member flaw through stable_initializer_of (see known-value-declaration). No certificate.

rules.name: known-value-budget
rules.derives: Whether a known value is available at all: budget exhaustion caches Failure::NodeLimit or PayloadLimit for the node and every later query in that file.
side_conditions: Work is cumulative per file in the order nodes are first queried (values.rs:312-324, primitive_values.rs:174-181).
Failure results are cached in state.values (values.rs:715-719).
Exhaustion maps to UnknownReason::ResourceExhaustion (values.rs:263-273).
rules.evidence: [S3] Spec §3.5 requires a node's state and cost identical in report and lint. Lint summarises only public roots (main.rs:284-291) while report summarises every reportable function (main.rs:147, 270), so the order and set of known_value queries differ. In a file with more than 4096 evaluated expression visits (or 1 MiB of reservations) a node that folds in lint can hit NodeLimit in report or the reverse, changing loop bounds and states. Counterexample shape: a file whose private functions issue more than 4096 known_value visits before `const K = 10` is first queried by public function `run`'s loop bound; report queries the private functions first, lint does not. This is by inspection, not executed. It also breaks 7.1 in spirit: the budget is per file, not per node.

rules.name: known-value-declaration
rules.derives: The value of an identifier or member access: the folded initializer of a const variable, an enum member, or a class `readonly` instance property that no member of the declaring class reassigns.
side_conditions: Const variable with a single identifier pattern and initializer (constants.rs:241-249).
Class member: PropertyDefinition with the TS `readonly` modifier and an initializer, and reassigns_key finds no write to that key in the declaring class body (values.rs:478-493, 1386-1407).
Receiver-to-class resolution by declared annotation (receivers.rs:23-140): `x: A` resolves x.n to A's member, `this.n` to the enclosing class's member, `new A().n` likewise.
rules.evidence: [S3] §2.5 says a value conforms to its declared type; TypeScript conformance is structural, and `readonly` is not part of the value's type. Counterexample: `class A { readonly n: number = 1; } export function f(a: A) { for (let i = 0; i < a.n; i++) {} }` with the call `f({ n: m })`, which is well-typed. member_of_receiver resolves `a.n` to A.n through the parameter annotation, constant_initializer_of accepts the readonly property, known_value folds a.n to 1, and the loop is costed O(1); the real count is m. The subclass form is also accepted: `class B extends A { readonly n: number; constructor(n: number) { super(); this.n = n; } }` overrides the field, `this.n` inside A's methods still folds to 1 because inherited_member_of never checks subclasses and reassigns_key inspects only A's body. The same fold gives Definedness::Defined or Undefined from an initializer. This is a stronger assumption than §2.5 (nominal, immutable, non-overridden property). Const variables and enum members are unaffected.

rules.name: known-value-fold
rules.derives: The primitive value (number, string, bigint, boolean, null, undefined) of an expression by constant folding: literals, parenthesised and TS wrappers, unary, binary, logical and sequence operators, string length, and identifiers or members that resolve to a known declaration.
side_conditions: The node belongs to the file's semantic (owns_node address check).
Depth below 64, at most 4096 node visits and 1 MiB cumulative reserved bytes per file, values at most 16384 bytes (primitive_values.rs:35-51).
Operators run through oxc_ecmascript constant evaluation over literal operands; in and instanceof, delete and lone surrogates are Unsupported.
Cycles return UncertifiedReference through the active set.
rules.evidence: [S3] Operators apply only to primitives, so no user code (valueOf, toString) runs; results rest on oxc_ecmascript matching the ECMAScript operator algorithms, an unmodelled external dependency the proof record would have to treat as an axiom or re-derive (§2.1 admits neither). Used by bounds.rs:822, budgets.rs:580, native.rs:1210, 1246, 3368. No certificate or named rule. Limits are per-file cumulative, see known-value-budget.

rules.name: primitive-length
rules.derives: The numeric `.length` of an array literal without spread (its element count), of a const identifier bound to an exact-size literal, or of a known string (UTF-16 units).
side_conditions: declaration_has_exact_size holds for identifiers (constant measure, and stable with no shrinking).
The container-visit budget.
rules.evidence: [S3] Exactness is checked through holder-stability with exact=true (shrink methods rejected). No certificate.

rules.name: declared-element-type
rules.derives: The element type of an iterable from `T[]`, `readonly T[]`, `Array<T>`, `ReadonlyArray<T>`, `Set<T>`, `ReadonlySet<T>` annotations, for-of variables and container members.
side_conditions: Type name recognised as global (element_of_type calls is_global_type_name, declared_types.rs:1387).
Annotation on the binding or the container member.
rules.evidence: [S3] Uses §2.5 only. Unlike declared-kind it checks the type name is global. No certificate.

rules.name: declared-kind
rules.derives: The Kind (Array, Set, Map, String, RegExp, Other, Unknown) of an expression from annotations, assertions, literals, `new`, calls' return annotations, and container member typings.
side_conditions: Depth at most 8 (containers 256).

Type references named Array, ReadonlyArray, Set, ReadonlySet, WeakSet, Map, ReadonlyMap, WeakMap, String, RegExp or a typed array are recognised by text (declared_types.rs:1788-1794, tables.rs:138-149) before any declaration lookup.
`new X()` with X named by text (declared_types.rs:1553).
`Object`, `Array` and `JSON` receivers are recognised by text in declared_type_of_call (1653-1666).
Methods join, toString, toLowerCase, toUpperCase, trim return String on any receiver (1681).
Type parameters use their constraint; any and unknown are Unknown; interfaces, classes, enums, type literals and object give Other.
rules.evidence: [S3] The recognised names are not checked against the global scope; is_global_type_name guards only the unresolved-name fallback (declared_types.rs:375-392) and element_of_type. named_kind_of runs before any declaration lookup (declared_types.rs:370-373), `new X` is matched by text (1551-1557) and `Object`/`Array`/`JSON` receivers by text (1650-1662). Counterexample (verified): `import { Set } from "lib"; export function f(s: Set<string>) { s.forEach((x) => {}); }` where lib's Set.forEach is quadratic. named_kind_of gives Kind::Set, member_of_receiver finds no analysed class for the external import, member dispatch sees no analysed-source `forEach`, so cost_of_call reaches native_of (walker.rs:2575-2589) and native_model_of(Identity::Receiver(Kind::Set), "forEach") models it Work::Linear(Operand::Receiver) (native.rs:497-500). The unknown remainder of an open target set with no known targets is not merged on this path (open_remainder_of's result is only retained into known targets, walker.rs:2519-2540). §2.2 constrains only replacement of built-ins, and a library class of the same name is not a built-in. The original `m.get(x)` example was wrong: Map `get` has no native model and falls to UnsupportedModel in cost_of_method_call (walker.rs:2821-2828). The local `const Array = {...}` shadowing case gives a wrong Kind, but calls on the result are still caught by program-wide member dispatch when their implementations are in analysed sources; it bites only when the result's methods come from outside the analysed sources. Kind is also fed by tsc answers, see receiver-kind. Verified (amended): Verdict upheld; counterexample replaced. Map.get is not modelled (native.rs models only set/delete/clear for Map; walker.rs:2821-2828 falls to UnsupportedModel), so the original example yields an unknown contribution. Set/Map forEach (Work::Linear) on an imported same-named class reproduces the defect. Local shadowing of `Array` is mitigated by member dispatch for analysed implementations.

rules.name: declared-primitive
rules.derives: An expression or binding is a primitive (or non-callable) value from annotations (`string`, `number`, literal types, enums, unions of these), literal and operator results, const write-free initializers, and, for parameters, the non-callable classification of every local call argument.
side_conditions: A union is primitive only if every part is (is_primitive_type).
Annotated variables and parameters additionally require is_proven_primitive_binding: not ambient, initializer non-callable, every write assigns a non-callable or is an update.
A parameter also needs the function's call sites to be all local and non-spread (call_arguments_of returns None for exported or imported functions).
Declared array element types give primitive elements (has_primitive_elements).
rules.evidence: [S3] Weaker than §2.5 for bindings (the call-site and write checks add conditions), so no reliance beyond the axiom found. Element sizes of `string[]` count as ONE (has_primitive_elements), which is an envelope assumption when strings are flattened or iterated. Feeds native cost selection (implicit-invocation avoidance for primitives). No named rule or certificate.

rules.name: declared-promise
rules.derives: An expression has declared type Promise or a union of Promise and primitives, so awaiting it is a native promise assimilation.
side_conditions: A reference named `Promise` is accepted by text (declared_types.rs:1210), aliases without type parameters are followed.
rules.evidence: [S3] The textual `Promise` match has the declared-kind name problem (S3-3 (G21)) and a structural thenable conforms to `Promise<T>` under §2.5 (its own `then` runs). Awaiting relies on the `then` dispatch check (AWAITED_MEMBERS) to catch analysed implementations. No certificate.

rules.name: kind-join
rules.derives: The Kind of a union, intersection, conditional or logical `||`/`??` expression: the part with the highest rank (Array 6, Set and Map 5, Unknown 4, String 3, RegExp 2, Other 1).
side_conditions: Fold starts at Other; ties keep the earlier kind.
An empty part list is Unknown.
rules.evidence: [S3] Rank order puts Unknown below Array, so `string[] | Foo` or `cond ? [] : mystery()` collapses to Kind::Array although §2.5 only says the value has one of the union's types. The effect is limited when another member-name dispatch (value_targets.rs) or is_intrinsic_member check catches user implementations, so no standalone counterexample is claimed; a union with a library-defined member outside the analysed sources loses soundness the same way as declared-kind.

rules.name: receiver-kind
rules.derives: A receiver's Kind: the declared kind, else, for methods that matter (method_matters), the TypeScript checker's type answer for the receiver span.
side_conditions: TscPass is Answering or Recording and the answer exists for the site key.
Answers arrive from the tsc sidecar (external process).
rules.evidence: [S3] The checker's static type is a declared type in the §2.5 sense. The kind label mapping lives in the sidecar (tsc_sidecar.mjs, slice 6), including whether it matches types by name (S3-3 (G21)). Delegated work must satisfy 7.1 (slice 6). No certificate.

rules.name: type-container
rules.derives: The type literal, interface, class or object literal that declares an expression's members, used to find member annotations.
side_conditions: `this` resolves to the nearest enclosing class ancestor (declared_types.rs:474-485).
Class members are searched in the declaring class only, not bases.
rules.evidence: [S3] `this` ignores intervening non-arrow functions, object-literal methods and static members, where `this` has a different declared type (§2.5 then names another type). Only member annotations are read from the result, so the effect is limited to wrong Kind or primitive claims in those positions.

rules.name: callee-resolution
rules.derives: The target function set and open/closed flag of a call: bindings via callable_reference, members via member_of_receiver, plus program-wide dispatch candidates, construction dispatch, and tsc callee answers.
side_conditions: An identifier is closed when it is write-free, has a determined runtime declaration and every alias step is closed (declarations.rs:306-420).
A member resolved through a declared receiver is never closed, and dispatch candidates add open targets (types.rs:210-247).
resolved_member_of returns closed=true for the declared-receiver member (types.rs:272-286).
rules.evidence: [S3] The identifier path is conservative when the file writes the binding. resolved_member_of (used at summaries.rs:2977 and walker.rs:2143) marks a member found through a declared receiver closed, which is unsound for a subclass or structural override of a getter or method; only those two call sites decide whether that reaches a cost. No certificate. Owned jointly with slice 2 (invocations, value_targets).

rules.name: class-construction-lineage
rules.derives: A `new C` call has a modelled Construction body (field initialisers) when no class in the chain declares a constructor and some class initialises an instance field.
side_conditions: The chain follows `extends` while class_of_expression resolves the base; the walk stops silently when the base is unresolved (declarations.rs:1049-1053).
Truncation is flagged only for cycles and MAXIMUM_LINEAGE.
rules.evidence: [S3] Candidate defect: a class extending an unresolved or external base (`class A extends ExternalBase { x = f(); }`) is classified as having no constructor in its lineage, so `new A()` is modelled as the field initialisers alone; whether walker.rs:1967-2046 adds an implicit super call for an unresolved base is not in this slice and must be confirmed in the refutation pass.

rules.name: name-resolution
rules.derives: The declaration a reference denotes, following imports, re-exports, star exports, namespace merging, CommonJS require and module.exports, and ambient globals, with an open flag for patched CommonJS modules.
side_conditions: oxc semantic scoping for local references.
Ambiguous global bindings across the same owner resolve to None (declarations.rs:1100-1142).
CommonJS files whose exports are patched, escape or are open are treated as open (patched_of, declarations.rs:2391-2523).
Module resolution through the project's resolver.
rules.evidence: [S3] Name resolution is a program-structure fact used by every family. The proof record must state (as a proof-record axiom Matt signs, or by modelling scoping) what a resolved reference denotes; §2.1 lists none. Direct eval and `with` can bind names the resolver does not see: is_write_free (declarations.rs:1148-1171) reads only the declaring file's resolved references and callable closure ignores eval and `with`; effects.rs:779 sets unknown_global for a direct eval call but no closure check consumes it here, so a top-level `eval(input)` that rewrites a closed function binding is a candidate hole to confirm in the refutation pass. Per-node cost: global_symbol_of (1100-1142) and patched_of (2391-2523) scan every project file on a miss, which conflicts with 7.1 and 7.2 (slice 6).

rules.name: surface-and-importers
rules.derives: Which bindings escape an entrypoint (exports, importers, surface writes and references) for public-surface and effect reasoning.
side_conditions: Export tables including star exports, CommonJS exports and TS namespaces.
surface_write_of classifies writes through reflective helpers (MUTATORS, REFLECTIVE_WRITES).
rules.evidence: [S3] Consumed by call_arguments_of (declared_types.rs:820-851) and public_surface.rs. No named rule or certificate.

rules.name: write-free-and-hoisting
rules.derives: A function or const binding is unwritten, and its runtime declarations are determined (a single hoisted function, no conflicting var initialisation or block-scoped duplicates), so calls through it are closed.
side_conditions: No resolved reference is a write, checked in the binding's own file.
Hoisted duplicates in the same scope, block-level function statements and var initialisers make it undetermined (declarations.rs:1173-1264).
rules.evidence: [S3] By inspection sound for ESM and single-file scopes. Writes through eval, `with`, `globalThis` and other files' unresolved references to a script-scope global are not observed here (see name-resolution).

gaps.summary: preference-rank is unsound: Part::max discards a lower-ranked part whatever its cost, and cost::nest carries an Absent preference onto factor*inner, so a loop whose body has no Normal part (typical above a budget-cancelled loop) becomes an Absent part that Reading::total or a later join drops. Fix nest (or cost_of_loop) to mark any part carrying cost as executed, and change the shipped expectation 'a while under two enclosing loops' => O(N) complete (tests/integration/budgets.rs:596-601), which exhibits the same loss.
gaps.counterexample: export function prefRank(n: number, xs: number[], ys: number[]): number { if (n >= 0 && n <= 1000000000) { let i = 0, total = 0; for (const x of xs) { for (const y of ys) { while (i < n && i >= 0) { i++; total += y; } } } return total; } return 0; } reports Known O(n) while the work is Theta(xs*ys) at n = 1 (reproduced, refute-1).

gaps.summary: budget-cancel amortises body executions against the potential but also removes each visit's first header evaluation (test, update, for-of next), folded into body_main at walker.rs:1446-1448, from the enclosing multiplication; only do-while bodies get a visit check. Keep the header reading per visit (multiplied by enclosing factors) apart from the amortised body, or require charge_covers(factor, visits) whenever the header costs more than O(1), and replace the Completion::Return device with an explicit amortised channel.
gaps.counterexample: function sum(xs: readonly number[]): number { let s = 0; for (const x of xs) s += x; return s; } export function cancelHeader(n: number, m: number, xs: number[]): number { if (n >= 0 && n <= 1000000000 && m >= 0 && m <= 1000000000) { let i = 0, c = 0; for (let j = 0; j < n; j++) { while (sum(xs) > j && i < m && i >= 0) { i++; c++; } } return c; } return 0; } reports Known O(m*xs) while the work is Theta(n*xs) at m = 1 (reproduced, refute-1).

gaps.summary: Share amortisation (budget-share, bound-share, share-sized-operation) assumes the shares spent within a visit sum to at most the potential, but the last share crosses the endpoint and can exceed it; the share is also granted from the default factor N of an unresolved bound (walker.rs:1389, 1424-1431). Charge potential + visits*max(share) with a bounded share and require a proven loop factor for granting; share-sized native calls and constructors follow the same charge. Remove the rule if that is not certifiable.
gaps.counterexample: export function shareOvershoot(n: number, m: number): number { if (n >= 0 && n <= 1000000000 && m >= 1 && m <= 1000000000) { let i = 0, steps = 0, t = 0; while (i < n && i >= 0 && steps < n && steps >= 0) { const k = m; for (let j = 0; j < k; j++) t++; i += k; steps++; } return t; } return 0; } reports Known O(n) while the work is Theta(m) at n = 1 (reproduced, refute-1).

gaps.summary: Work under an unknown multiplicity is counted once in the printed partial cost, and lint fails on that cost (main.rs:328-334), so Exceeds can come from a value that is not a floor. Paths: loop-unbounded and nest's overflow fallback (walker.rs:1566-1590, body_main.scaled(None) leaves the cost), iteration with unknown count (invocations.rs:752-763), native visits (native.rs:2694-2703), escaped lazy work and untracked latent consumption. The signed spec rejected counting an unknown multiplicity as one pass: such a contribution adds zero to the floor and keeps its unknowns. Tests bounds.rs:899-909 and walker.rs:1528-1549 (including do-while) pin the current behaviour and change with the fix.
gaps.counterexample: export function unbounded(xs: number[]): number { let c = 0; let k = 1; while (k !== xs.length) { for (const a of xs) for (const b of xs) c += a * b; k = (k * 3) % 7; } return c; } with max O(N) reports `O(xs^2) [partial] > O(N)` and lint exits 1, although the while may run zero times (reproduced, refute-1).

gaps.summary: Untracked sizes and multiplicities default to the input envelope Cost::N (LegacyN), which bind_cost_in binds to max(entry root sizes) or a placeholder dimension when no input is sized; this is an assumption outside §2 and not an input dimension. Entry points: Size::sized and input_size_of marking element Cost::N resolved (values.rs:141-149, 1015-1029), the default method factor (walker.rs:2729-2731), report.rs:134, iteration_count_at's count_of(...).unwrap_or(Cost::N) (invocations.rs:2854), unknown_visits_part_of and rest reads scaling unknown parts by N (invocations.rs:408, 1550), bound-for-in's N for open objects, bound-live-visits' max(N, budget) (bounds.rs:300), linear_bound_of (bounds.rs:2247), for-of-produced-length keeping factor N, the share-grant factor, Potential::Enveloped, bound-linear-default, legacy LOG and summaries.rs:5510. Replace each with a tracked size or an unknown SizeRelation/multiplicity contribution; the lowerings fall under the §5.7 certificate exemption, so no disproof is needed. Plan action 4.4 already prescribes this outcome, so S3-1's decide is settled by the plan.
gaps.counterexample: const buf: number[] = []; export function fill(a: number[]) { for (const x of a) for (const y of a) buf.push(x * y); } export function drain() { for (const v of buf) {} } charges drain O(N) while it does n^2 work after fill(a) with |a| = n. Also: nest(a: number[][]) with a nested for-of reports Known O(max(1, a^2)) while one K-element inner array costs Theta(K); scan() over a module-level store reports Known O(N) with no input; a for-in over an object filled with xs^2 keys claims O(N) (reproduced, refute-1 and refute-2).

gaps.summary: Map set/delete/clear and Set add/delete/clear are Work::Constant (native.rs:457-496) and Set/Map construction is charged linear, while ECMA-262 24.1.3.9, 24.1.3.3, 24.2.4.1 and 24.2.4.4 scan [[MapData]]/[[SetData]] with For-each loops, clear visits every entry, and AddEntriesFromIterable calls the adder per element (O(n^2) construction). Map get/has and Set has fall to UnsupportedModel although is_modelled counts them modelled. The signed spec rejected amortized constant keyed access, so model every keyed method Linear(Receiver), construction quadratic, add WeakMap/WeakSet kinds, and update the tests that pin constant add/set/delete (budgets.rs:701-884, effects.rs:325-341, walker.rs, native.rs, model goldens).
gaps.note: S4-7's remaining part (Array push/pop/at and String at/charAt/charCodeAt left unmodelled) is G45.

gaps.summary: Object.groupBy and Map.groupBy run GroupBy (7.3.35), whose AddValueToKeyedGroup (7.3.34) scans the groups List per element: O(n*g) steps, up to Theta(n^2), charged Linear(First) (native.rs:258-271). With keyed access decided linear by the signed spec (G6), charge the product.

Array and %TypedArray% sort/toSorted are charged N log N (comparator N log N times), but SortIndexedProperties (23.1.3.30.1) uses an implementation-defined sequence of SortCompare calls, so §2.4 makes the contribution and its callback work unknown. The signed spec rejected an O(n log n) sort axiom. Tests walker.rs:221, native.rs:339 and the model goldens (expected-report.txt:39-45, 53-61: breakInsideLoop, returnInsideLoop, usesPathAlias, sharedFn, sortMethodCall) change with the fix; ARRAY_N_LOG_N goes once empty.
locations: tests/fixtures/model/expected-report.txt:11,19,39-45,53-61 (branches.ts:119,130; methods.ts:6; lib/shared.ts:2 via sharedFn and usesPathAlias)
gaps.counterexample: a.slice().sort(cmp) reports Known O(a log a) (reproduced with the binary, refute-4).

gaps.summary: String localeCompare (22.1.3.12, implementation-defined locale comparison) and toLocaleLowerCase/toLocaleUpperCase (22.1.3.26/.27, host-locale result) are modelled Linear(Receiver) through STRING_LINEAR (tables.rs:88-91); §2.4 makes them unknown contributions. localeCompare also ignores the argument's length.
gaps.counterexample: s.localeCompare(t) reports Known O(max(s,t)) (reproduced with the binary, refute-4).

gaps.summary: String search with a string needle (includes, indexOf, lastIndexOf, split, replace, replaceAll) is charged one Cost::N, which reports as the max of receiver and needle dimensions, while StringIndexOf (6.1.4.1) and the lastIndexOf loop compare a searchLen substring at each candidate: O((n-m+1)*m), up to Theta(n^2). Charge the product of receiver and needle sizes. startsWith/endsWith are O(min(n,m)) and compliant. Per-candidate equality cost depends on G52.
gaps.counterexample: s.includes(t) reports O(max(t, s)) while StringIndexOf does Theta(s*t) at |t| = |s|/2 (reproduced with the binary, refute-4).

gaps.summary: replaceAll (22.1.3.20) and global-regex replace (22.2.6.11) run GetSubstitution per match, building n + k*|replacement|, but are charged one linear factor. Callback return values are ToString-coerced per match with no charge (invoke_callback, native.rs:1445-1449). A single-match replace, O(n + r), is covered.
gaps.counterexample: s.replaceAll('a', r) reports O(max(s,r)) while the work is Theta(s*r) when every code unit matches (reproduced with the binary, refute-4).

gaps.summary: Array.prototype.join (23.1.3.18) is charged the receiver length (ARRAY_LINEAR, tables.rs:25), but its output is the sum of element-string lengths plus (n-1)*|sep|, and each ToString may invoke user toString/valueOf/@@toPrimitive on object elements, none of which is charged.

map, filter, slice, splice, flat and flatMap call ArraySpeciesCreate (10.4.2.3), and TypedArray map/filter/slice/subarray call TypedArraySpeciesCreate (23.2.4.1), which read constructor and @@species and Construct the result, running user code for subclass instances that conform under §2.5. Only concat prices species (native.rs:2001-2105).

The walker's Receiver branch skips argument coercions the steps perform: ToIntegerOrInfinity on index arguments of includes, indexOf, lastIndexOf, slice, splice, fill, copyWithin and with; ToString on the RegExp exec/test argument; ToString on elements in default-comparator sort. Each may call user valueOf/toString/@@toPrimitive.

Set union/intersection/difference/symmetricDifference/isSubsetOf/isSupersetOf/isDisjointFrom are charged a flat Cost::N (walker.rs:2770-2790), but GetSetRecord invokes the argument's user-definable size getter, has and keys, the steps iterate other.keys() or call other.has per element, and dedupe by SetDataHas List scans. Neither the other operand's size nor its user methods are charged.

JSON.stringify is charged N over the value graph, but with a space argument SerializeJSONObject/Array emit indent per line growing with depth, Theta(N*depth) output (Theta(N^2) for a chain), and the [[Stack]] contains check is an O(depth) List scan per object. serialized_part_of (native.rs:2487-2545) reads only the replacer.

JSON.parse with a reviver charges the reviver per element of the text, but InternalizeJSONProperty (25.5.1.1) reads each key after earlier siblings' reviver calls, so a reviver writing holder[laterKey] can graft arbitrarily large or cyclic values. Charge an unknown unless the reviver provably never writes its holder (arrow and this-free revivers are exempt).

The LINEAR_CONSTRUCTORS fallback, reached only for unresolved construction targets with no intrinsic model, matches `new C(x)` by bare name without the intrinsic_replaced_of check the model path makes (walker.rs:2053) and adds no unknown. WeakSet/WeakMap constructors iterate through the user iterator protocol and call the adder per element uncharged; ArrayBuffer/SharedArrayBuffer and TypedArray(length) do work proportional to a numeric value. Plan action 4.1 adds WeakMap/WeakSet kinds but not this fallback.
gaps.counterexample: A parameter named Map typed MapConstructor makes `new Map(xs)` Known O(N) with no unknown (another parameter name draws an unknown target), and `new WeakSet(xs)` is Known O(xs) (reproduced with the binary, refute-4).

gaps.summary: For literal regex patterns searched_part_of returns empty (native.rs:1530-1534), but String replace/split/match/matchAll/search dispatch to RegExp.prototype[@@...], which Get exec, flags, lastIndex and, for split/matchAll, SpeciesConstructor; §2.2 lets the analysed program replace them. No builtin_members_replaced(Kind::RegExp, ..) check exists. Detect replacement of these members or charge them.

Matching::Once is applied to RegExp test/exec and to match/search with g or y flags (walker.rs:2792-2822), where exec starts at lastIndex and lookbehind, \b and ^ observe the prefix; the is_context_free guard protects only the Repeated path. Apply the guard (or charge the lastIndex scan of RegExpBuiltinExec step 13) on the Once path. Split from S4-22, whose oracle question is G47.

Built-in kinds are recognised by type or callee name without checking the name is the global: named_kind_of runs before declaration lookup (declared_types.rs:370-373), `new X` and Object/Array/JSON receivers are matched by text, Promise by text, and the String-returning method list applies to any receiver (1674). A same-named imported class gets the built-in cost model with no unknown. Require the name to resolve to no local symbol before assigning a built-in kind, and apply STRING_RESULTS only to receivers already Kind::String.
gaps.counterexample: import { Set } from "lib"; export function f(s: Set<string>) { s.forEach((x) => {}); } models lib's (possibly quadratic) forEach as Work::Linear(Receiver) with no unknown (traced at HEAD).

gaps.summary: known_value folds a class `readonly` instance property to its initializer through the receiver's declared class, but structural typing and subclass fields let any conforming value stand there (§2.5), and readonly is not part of the value's type. Drop the class-member arm of constant_initializer_of (keep const variables and enum members) or fold only for provably closed classes.
gaps.counterexample: class A { readonly n: number = 1; } export function f(a: A) { for (let i = 0; i < a.n; i++) {} } costs the loop O(1) while the well-typed call f({ n: m }) runs m iterations; a subclass overriding n in its constructor folds the same way (traced at HEAD).

gaps.summary: Implicit invocation (getters, setters, coercion hooks including declared valueOf/toString, @@hasInstance, iterator protocol accessors, a `then` getter) closes its target set from an index of program syntax alone, so values entering from outside the analysed program are assumed to carry no accessors or hooks; §2.5 admits them and §2 has no axiom excluding them. Either open the set for receivers that are unresolved or come from inputs, or Matt signs an axiom that entry inputs carry no accessors or protocol hooks. The `then` call on an input is already open; only a `then` getter stays closed inside an already Partial node.
gaps.counterexample: export function f(o: { x: number }): number { return o.x; } is Known O(1), but a conforming caller passes an object whose getter x loops this.n times; `${o}`, o instanceof C and +o with o: { valueOf(): number } are likewise Known O(1) (reproduced, refute-2 p1/p2).
gaps.decision: Matt, 2026-09-29: Keep the closed world for accessors and protocol hooks on inputs; the results rest on a §2 axiom drafted for Matt to sign (inputs carry no accessors or hooks beyond those the analysed program defines). Until signed, these rule applications stay uncertified.

gaps.summary: Array iteration steps loop to LengthOfArrayLike (up to 2^53-1, holes included), not to the populated element count, so new Array(n), a.length = n and sparse arrays make forEach/map/indexOf/join do work in a numeric value. Verify with the family-H produced-size rules that produced length tracks the `length` value; where it tracks populated elements, the size is untracked and becomes unknown under G5. §2.3 fixes the step count, so the slice's decide is a verification task.

Union, intersection, conditional and ||/?? kinds collapse to the highest-ranked part (Array 6 and Set/Map 5 outrank Unknown 4, declared_types.rs:31-51, 136-146), while §2.5 gives only that the value has one of the parts' types. Join to Kind::Unknown unless all parts agree. Member dispatch catches analysed implementations, so only values from outside the analysed sources are affected.

container_of_expression resolves `this` to the nearest Class ancestor (declared_types.rs:476-485), crossing non-arrow functions, object-literal methods and static members whose `this` differs. Stop at the first non-arrow function boundary and respect static placement.

resolved_member_of marks a member found through a declared receiver closed and adds no member-dispatch candidates (types.rs:272-293); through construction_targets_of, `new a.C()` keeps a single declared target closed when a structural value's C comes from outside the analysed sources. Pass closed=false as resolved_expression_callee_of does.

Callable closure (callable_reference, is_write_free, runtime_declarations_of, declarations.rs:306-420, 1148-1171) never consults direct eval or `with`, so a module-level function called after eval(code) stays a closed target although strict direct eval can reassign that binding; unknown_global invalidates only loops containing the eval. Treat every non-const binding reachable from a direct-eval or with scope as open (has_direct_eval exists at value_sizes.rs:261), or report an unknown contribution at such calls.

Regex classification depends on wall-clock budgets: a 10 s per-pattern timeout sent to recheck (regex.rs:332, regex_sidecar.mjs:73), a 120 s batch deadline measured with Instant (regex.rs:411-446) that marks remaining patterns Exhausted, and status polling with sleep; tests (regex.rs:469, 591, 731-749) pin a 3 s helper deadline, a 32 MB heap cap, a ZERO timeout and a 10000 ms request timeout. Identical inputs can give different states (§3.4). Replace with deterministic size or step budgets and treat the process deadline as a hard failure; the §7.2 attribution of recheck work belongs to action 6.1.

Scheduling iterates std HashSet with per-process RandomState: publish_task wakes waiters in hash order (summaries.rs:1333-1343) and finish_components adds SCC edges in hash order of each task's dependencies (1539-1556). Queue order decides which dependencies are Ready, how many passes and charges occur, which specializations the per-function cap admits and where the global budget exhausts, so work counts and near-budget states can differ between identical runs (§3.4). Use ordered collections or sort before iterating.

No per-entry verdict exists: CostComparison orders costs only and ignores the entry's state, so a Partial or Unknown entry under the limit is treated as Within, and Inconclusive is approximated by a Comparison unknown appended only for incomparable costs (main.rs:290-317, 329-334). Form Within (Known and proven at or below), Exceeds (bound or floor proven above, ceilings later) and Inconclusive per entry to drive lint and the error policy.

State differs between lint and report: lint joins a Comparison unknown into a Known incomparable entry while report keeps it Known; report uses summarize_with(raw=true) for functions with a function-level @perf cost, skipping the directive branch, so it prints the derived body cost where lint uses the directive cost (also a §3.3 break); report adds envelope-binding ResourceExhaustion only in report; and lint analyses public_roots while report analyses reportable() plus explicit roots under the shared global admission caps, so a cap can trip in one mode only. Add a corpus-wide report-versus-lint equality test; the cap coupling resolves with G67.
gaps.counterexample: tests/fixtures/model/expected-report.txt:84 prints 'O(max(1, (xs * xs^2))) nlognFunctionTagged [@perf O(N log N)]' while lint uses O(N log N).

gaps.summary: No asserted marker propagates: only a function-level @perf cost directive is marked in the report (report.rs:110-126), Part has no assertion field, and ignore, bounded, hot, cold, statement-level cost and callers of asserted callees reach dependents as ordinary cost, so they are neither marked (§4.7) nor excluded from raises (§5.6). The working tree's uncommitted asserted-summary tracking must be checked to cover ignore and hot/cold before this closes.

No Unknown state is rendered: an all-unknown node prints its default cost as 'O(1) [partial]', floor and bound are not distinguished, and unknown origins appear only as stderr diagnostics that the ignore policy suppresses, so the report omits the §4.7 origins under ignore (report.rs:339-366, main.rs:359-383). §4.7 and §4.9 require origins in a report identical under every policy; only the rendering format is drafted for Matt.

finish_reading tags every bind failure of a callee channel (UnknownName, UnresolvedQuantity, Domain) as ResourceExhaustion and leaves the part's unbound callee-scope cost (summaries.rs:574-588), misreporting a semantic gap as a §7 lowering and letting the unbound cost enter the printed partial cost.

Under the literal steps [[MapData]]/[[SetData]] never shrink: delete and clear write ~empty~ in place, so forEach, the iterators and every keyed scan walk every entry ever inserted. The live-size charges in native-visit-budget (live_visits_of, effects.rs:1583) and the for-of/collection sizing undercut this when deletions occur.
gaps.decision: Matt, 2026-09-29: Follow the literal steps: deleted entries stay in [[MapData]]/[[SetData]], so after a delete or clear the scanned size is untracked and unknown.

gaps.summary: String normalize (UAX #15, canonical reordering quadratic per run of combining marks), toLowerCase/toUpperCase (Unicode Default Case Conversion, bounded expansion) and the trim family (WhiteSpace property data) delegate to Unicode rather than ECMAScript steps, and are modelled Linear(Receiver) (tables.rs:83-87, 90). Decide whether Unicode-delegated work is unknown or covered by a signed Unicode axiom; normalize's Linear charge undercuts even the delegated worst case.
gaps.decision: Matt, 2026-09-29: Unknown contributions under §2.4; no Unicode axiom.

gaps.summary: JSON.parse's parse step validates per ECMA-404 and uses ParseText, which specify grammar, not algorithm steps; the Linear(First) charge assumes a linear parse and O(1) CreateDataPropertyOrThrow per member. Decide whether grammar-defined parsing is linear by axiom or unknown.
gaps.decision: Matt, 2026-09-29: JSON.parse parse step is an unknown contribution under §2.4.

gaps.summary: Buffer.from/concat/alloc/allocUnsafe/compare (Node.js) and structuredClone (HTML) are host APIs with no ECMA-262 steps; their Linear models (native.rs:290-327) rest on no signed axiom. Make them unknown or have Matt sign a host axiom.
gaps.decision: Matt, 2026-09-29: Host APIs (Buffer, structuredClone) are unknown contributions.

gaps.summary: A @perf cost directive naming a quantity the specialisation cannot resolve yields the directive cost plus a SizeRelation unknown (Partial, walker.rs:479-497, summaries.rs:2424-2436), and a directive whose binding hits Resource/Overflow becomes an Unknown ResourceExhaustion node (walker.rs:455-461, summaries.rs:2391-2401), while §3.3 makes a directive-set node Known with that cost. Decide whether an unresolvable directive is a directive error (diagnostic plus Unknown) or Known with the unbound cost.
gaps.decision: Matt, 2026-09-29: An unresolvable directive quantity is a directive error: diagnostic plus Unknown. An overflowing binding is Known with the directive cost (§3.3).

gaps.summary: Diagnostics are per unknown origin, not per Inconclusive entry, and under error the exit code depends on any selected origin (main.rs:356), including public-coverage origins pushed at main.rs:260 that belong to no entry. §4.6 fails lint only for Inconclusive entries while §4.9 gives unknown origins an error diagnostic; decide whether an entry-less origin fails lint under error.
gaps.decision: Matt, 2026-09-29: Under error, lint fails only for Inconclusive entries (§4.6); every unknown origin still draws an error diagnostic (§4.9).

gaps.summary: TypeMode::Auto falls back to declarations-only typing when node or typescript is unavailable (main.rs:213-224), changing node states by environment with only a stderr note. §1's analysed program includes files a delegated tool reads, so a missing typescript arguably changes the input rather than breaking §3.4; decide whether Auto may fall back.
gaps.decision: Matt, 2026-09-29: TypeMode::Auto exits 2 when node or typescript is unavailable; syntactic typing stays an explicit flag.

gaps.summary: Exceeds lines print '<cost>[ [partial]] > <limit>' (report.rs:204-216) and state neither that the value is what olint proves, nor whether it is a bound or floor, nor that an instance's work may fall below it (§4.4).

Conservative open alternatives (catch discovery open for every non-throw origin, unknown serialization shapes, unresolved write-occurrence frequency) are sound unknown contributions; what remains is a §4.7 test that each carries a source origin in the report and is covered by a fixture.

Array push/pop/at and String at/charAt/charCodeAt fall to UnsupportedModel (walker.rs:2824-2831, tables.rs:54-67) although their steps are fully specified and O(1); sound but conservative, and modelling them would raise nodes. Split from S4-7, whose Map/Set part is G6.
gaps.decision: Matt, 2026-09-29: Model Array push/pop/at and String at/charAt/charCodeAt as constant under §2.3.

gaps.summary: No rule in any family has a rule name, recorded side conditions, a certificate or a Lean soundness theorem (§6.1, §6.4, §6.5): families A-D (slice 1), E/F/I/J (slice 2), H size derivations (slice 3), G built-ins (slice 4), and the review's PASS offers no §6 evidence. Certificates attach at Part::max, nest, Bound::Proven, the recurrence solution, bind_cost_in, the escape lift and the native reading. Rules that phase 4 fixes certify only after those fixes.
gaps.note: Action 5.1 builds the derivation arena these certificates need.

gaps.summary: regex-cost rests on recheck 4.5.0's automaton classification, an external oracle outside the signed axioms: its degree must bound the Pattern-semantics step count of RegExpBuiltinExec including the lastIndex scan, from a nonzero lastIndex too. Plan action 5.5 and the plan's Risks settle the route: a Lean-checkable witness, failing that regex bounds become unknown under §5.7; restricting to a proven fragment is the middle option.

Explanations lose derivation content: Part::max keeps only the selected side's trace unless Inconclusive (cost.rs:1800-1863), a loop bound's proof is one &'static str, recurrence solutions carry a proof string, labels are free text ('@perf <cost>', bound word, budget suffix), a ONE-cost directive draws no trace node, and Known-bound steps are not distinguished from proven floor contributions (§6.5).

The cost domain carries conventions the Lean model must fix: every Size dimension counts as at least 1, Log(x) counts as at least 1 and positive even for log(1) = 0 (legacy LOG with no roots, log of a constant measure), a product with constant 0 collapses to 0, and Log of a Ratio below 1 passes validity (cost.rs:319-321, 601, 617, 690-698, 1068-1082, 1213-1217). Decide whether costs read as max(1, .), which makes these sound, or the constructors are rewritten.
gaps.decision: Matt, 2026-09-29: Every cost reads as max(1, ·) in the proof record.

gaps.summary: Soundness of bound-additive/constant-distance (rounding headroom), bound-exact-additive (quarter units within 2^48), bound-geometric downward (termination by underflow), bound-bisection (int32 >> within 2^30) and rec-relation/rec-guard (x - 1 == x above 2^53, ToInt32) rests on IEEE-754 double and ToInt32 semantics. Decide that the proof record's work model encodes ECMAScript Number semantics rather than idealised integers or reals.
gaps.decision: Matt, 2026-09-29: The proof record encodes ECMAScript Number semantics (IEEE-754 double, ToInt32).

gaps.summary: Declared-type facts (kind, primitive, element type, promise, container member typings, tsc answers) and name resolution are program-structure facts every family consumes. §2.5 states only conformance and §6.2 reserves the model to Matt: decide how the proof record encodes TypeScript types, structural conformance and scoping, and whether these facts carry certificates.
gaps.decision: Matt, 2026-09-29: Declared-type facts enter certificates as premises justified by §2.5; name resolution is recomputed in Lean from the encoded syntax.

gaps.summary: The work of spec-internal operations the steps use without loops is undefined in the axioms: string concatenation (join, JSON output, GetSubstitution), List append/contains (JSON stack, PropertyList), String and BigInt equality (SameValueZero, IsStrictlyEqual: O(length) per comparison, charged O(1) in includes, indexOf and keyed lookups), ordinary-object property lookup and OrdinaryOwnPropertyKeys ordering (Object.keys/values/entries/assign/freeze). The proof record's work model must fix these costs before built-in certificates, and the equality answer feeds phase 4 charges (G10, G6).
gaps.decision: Matt, 2026-09-29: Spec-internal operation costs rest on a small §2 axiom set drafted for Matt to sign: property lookup O(1), List append O(1), List contains O(length), String concatenation and equality O(length), BigInt equality O(digits), OrdinaryOwnPropertyKeys unknown.

gaps.summary: Value folding (known-value-fold, primitive-length, definedness, value-identity) has no rule names, certificates or theorems, and delegates operator semantics to oxc_ecmascript, an outside implementation that is neither a §2 axiom nor derivable in the proof record. Certify against a Lean model of the ECMAScript primitive operators, or restrict the evaluator to operators the model covers.

Bound and budget side conditions are established across two modules: write_sites_of, is_stable_endpoint, writes_of and is_invariant see only direct binding writes, and loop_invalidation_of (effects.rs:808-866) covers nested functions, aliases and member writes. Certificates for bound-additive, bound-constant-distance, bound-progression and budget-collect must carry the effects facts as premises, or the rules must check them locally.

rec-markers multiplies each edge's marker coefficient by the recorded call-site count, but only invocation_reading_of records sites; the latent cyclic branch (summaries.rs:5393-5404) records none. State and prove that every marker-contributing edge is walked through invocation_reading_of, or record steps on the latent path.

call-fallback reuses the merged readings of specialisations observed at a site on earlier passes; soundness needs the unstated invariant that the fallback pass would compute one of those keys, which holds only if the site's argument facts did not depend on missing or exhausted dependencies at observation. State and prove it, or re-key fallback reuse on the current facts.

Recurrence edge lower bounds and argument ranges are f64 (min-folded, summaries.rs:6080-6111; recurrences.rs:97-113). A Lean certificate needs exact side conditions: emit them as exact dyadic rationals or re-derive them in the checker.

No test covers the proof machinery: no certificate emission or acceptance check, no assertion that explanations name rules and side conditions, no ceilings or instance families, no dead-end regression fixtures, no rank comparison (§5.1) and no recorded project sweep; proofs/ is absent from olint HEAD. Phases 1, 5 and 7 build these; this gap is closed when each has a test.
locations: proofs/ (absent at HEAD ce0cb54; the untracked working-tree proofs/ is Phase 3 in progress)
gaps.note: Pieces land in actions 1.3 (rank diff), 1.5 (dead ends), 5.1-5.4 (certificates) and 7.3 (ceilings).

gaps.summary: The tsc recording loop (summaries.rs:4813-4850) has no round cap: each round resets every summary and the scheduler (reset_between_passes also renews the WorkBudget, so the budget caps nothing), re-runs public discovery and re-summarises every reportable function, and rounds are bounded only by dependent sites + 1 = O(|G|), giving Theta(n^2) walker work. The regex recording loop sits inside an outer main loop that re-runs tsc and regex gathering until the regex answer count stops growing, multiplying passes when the program has regex literals. Walk each node a constant number of times, re-summarising only functions with newly answered sites.
gaps.counterexample: Family rounds: function mk_i(){ return { r: d_i } } and function d_i(v){ return mk_{i+1}().r(v) } for i < n, plus export function selected(v){ return mk_0().r(v) }, with each mk_i's return hidden from olint's own value tracking (as the `make(): any` of analysis_scaling.rs:2875-2919 does) but visible to tsc: n+1 rounds over O(n) functions. Put a regex literal in each d_i to multiply outer iterations.

gaps.summary: The primitive evaluator's node, byte and payload budgets are cumulative per file, consumed in query order and cached per node (values.rs:312-324, 715-719; primitive_values.rs:156-163). Lint queries public roots only while report queries every reportable function, so a node can fold in one mode and be Unknown (ResourceExhaustion) in the other (§3.5). Bound each evaluation by a per-root, per-expression budget independent of query order, charged to the queried node.
gaps.counterexample: A file whose private functions issue more than 4096 known_value visits before `const K = 10` is first queried by public run's loop bound: report exhausts before reaching K, lint does not (by inspection).

gaps.summary: Each recording round spawns a fresh node process that runs ts.createProgram (parse and bind of every root, lib and referenced file) per configuration and rebuilds checker and span indexes (tsc.rs:117-155, tsc_sidecar.mjs:301-317): Theta(|G|) delegated work per round and Theta(R*|G|) in total. The exchange has no wall-time or heap bound, so delegated memory is unaccounted.
gaps.counterexample: Under the rounds family of {recording-loops}, delegated checker work is Theta(n^2).

gaps.summary: Per-query checker work grows with program size and is uncounted: kindOfType recurses over every union member, isStructuralObject walks union/intersection members, index infos and properties, the tuple check maps every union member, candidatesOf scans all members of each class declaration, and implementationsOf rescans every sibling declaration per bodiless declaration (tsc_sidecar.mjs:86-115, 201-237, 297).
gaps.counterexample: (a) type U = A_1|...|A_n with n sites needing a type query: Theta(n^2). (b) namespace N { export class K { m_1(){} ... m_n(){} } } with n sites new N.K() olint does not resolve itself: Theta(n^2). (c) declare const o: C_1|...|C_n called as o.m() at n sites: Theta(n^2) reply size and memory. (d) n overloads of f plus one implementation with n sites x.f(): each overload calls implementationsOf over all n declarations, Theta(n^2) per query, Theta(n^3) total.

gaps.summary: No unit of work or memory is attributed to a node (§7.2): charges carry an event only (analysis_work.rs:64-90), charge_work takes no node (summaries.rs:935-1011), children_of charges a whole file's node count as GraphNode to the first caller (walker.rs:303-313), task admission reserves by body size per task (summaries.rs:1092-1127), and sidecar and regex helper work is per batch.

function_may_schedule does not cache results computed while a cycle is active (effects.rs:1573-1578), so a call graph with back edges re-explores callees along every path up to depth 64, each also re-running counted_subtree, until the global EffectPrepassNode budget stops it.
gaps.counterexample: g_i calls g_{i+1} and g_{i+2}, each g_i also calls g_1, all reached from an async loop's pending-effect scan: Fibonacci-many visits up to the depth cap.

gaps.summary: tsconfig extends loading removes each path from visited after loading (tsconfig.rs:767) with no memo, so a diamond or repeated parent reloads along every path, and each referenced project re-parses its whole extends chain in select_project.
gaps.counterexample: c_i.json {"extends": ["./c_{i+1}.json", "./c_{i+1}.json"]} for i < n makes 2^n loads; n references sharing a chain of length L cost Theta(n*L).

gaps.summary: Include glob matching backtracks without memoization: include_matches branches on each ** and wildcard_matches/star_matches retry every split per * (tsconfig.rs:329-347, 427-496).
gaps.counterexample: include "a/**/**/.../**/*.ts" with k ** over a depth-k tree costs about C(2k,k) per path; include "src/*a*a...*a*b.ts" with k stars against names a^m.ts costs Theta(m^k) per file.

gaps.summary: Program-global per-pass caps turn constant-work nodes Unknown(ResourceExhaustion) once the rest of the program has consumed them, with no scaling family showing the node's own counts growing (§7.4) and no attribution of the spent work: the WorkBudget (uniform 4,000,000 per event; TaskKey 20,000, BodyPass 100,000, CallbackDescriptor 20,000, RecurrenceContext 4096, CaptureEdge 200,000; summaries.rs:262-280), the trace arena (1M nodes, 64 MiB), public discovery (100k steps), IMPLEMENTATION_FILE_LIMIT 4096 and regex patterns per batch (1024). Many tests assert these cap-driven lowerings (analysis_scaling.rs, walker.rs, summary_fallback.rs, analysis_work.test.rs, cost.test.rs, enum_values.test.rs). Decide how to conform: per-node charge limits shown constant by scaling families, removal of caps on events already linear, or a whole-run failure in place of per-node demotion.
gaps.counterexample: n independent `export function f_i(){ return i }` exceed TaskKey 20,000, and later nodes lose their bound although per-node work is constant (confirmed statically).
gaps.decision: Matt, 2026-09-29: Program-global caps become per-node charge limits backed by scaling families; a global limit remains only as a whole-run failure (exit 2) that never demotes nodes.

gaps.summary: drive_summaries calls finish_components whenever the queue drains with tasks waiting, and each call rebuilds the dependency graph over all waiting tasks and reruns Kosaraju (summaries.rs:1517-1616); a non-cyclic component is only enqueued in that wave, so a chain alternating cyclic components and acyclic waiting tasks resolves one link per wave: Theta(n^2) GraphNode/GraphEdge, then exhaustion.
gaps.counterexample: g_i(x){ if(x) g_i(x-1); return a_i(x) } with a_i(x){ return g_{i+1}(x) }: Theta(n) waves over a Theta(n) graph.

gaps.summary: Per-call and per-reference steps are not constant per node: function_inputs walks every enclosing scope's parameters per call (summaries.rs:380-447), key_of clones and canonicalises all substitutions and latent channel keys per invocation and hashes the full SummaryKey per lookup, captured_substitutions_of scans all current substitutions, is_tracked_consumption recurses over all references to depth 6 (fan-out R^6, summaries.rs:5828-5836), and complete_recurrence enumerates up to 4096 contexts per component. The global budget masks the growth.

Recurrence-member sets propagate from each Ready callee into its caller (summaries.rs:1228-1237) and are unioned by copy (Arc::make_mut plus extend, 1780-1806), so time and memory are Theta(n^2) on a caller chain, and past the cap callers fall to ResourceExhaustion, making states depend on n.
gaps.counterexample: r_i(x){ if(x) r_i(x-1) } and c_i(){ r_i(1); c_{i+1}() }: c_1's set holds all n r_i.

gaps.summary: Each loop the walker reaches calls loop_invalidation_of (walker.rs:1380), which re-runs the effect prepass over the loop's whole body with no per-loop cache (effects.rs:1697-1725), and invalidation_of walks all ancestors per loop (1888-1918), so nested loops re-scan inner bodies at every level. The existing nested-iteration test measures only iterator exits and DispatchStep.
gaps.counterexample: n nested for (let i_k=0;i_k<m;i_k++) { ... x++ }: Theta(n^2) EffectPrepassNode and ancestor steps.

gaps.summary: Effect and storage sets are Vecs merged by linear contains with no charge: Effects::join (effects.rs:359-379), push_binding/push_value (404-414), Storage::merge (306-319) and the may_alias scan (1956-1964) cost O(|a|*|b|), repeated per specialization and round.
gaps.counterexample: n module-level let a_i all written in one exported function (a_1=1; ...; a_n=n;): Theta(n^2) comparisons per walk.

gaps.summary: Callee targets are deduplicated with Vec::contains in resolved_of_callee_answer (types.rs:423-433), push_known (484-488) and the dispatch merge (250-257): Theta(k^2) per call site in the target count k, re-resolved every pass.
gaps.counterexample: With the union-receiver family ({checker-per-query} (c)), k = n at n sites: Theta(n^3).

gaps.summary: Project loading scans the open-file stack linearly on every import (project.rs:398-402, 430-437), every configuration re-walks and re-resolves each shared file (290-352, 404-421), and owners, conditions_of and jsx_runtime_in scan owner lists.
gaps.counterexample: n files where file_i imports file_{i+1} and file_0: Theta(n^2); n project references including the same m files: Theta(n*m) resolutions.

gaps.summary: Public-surface discovery repeats work: visited is cleared per entrypoint (public_surface.rs:104-107), issue() dedups with Vec::contains (176-182), the limit merge scans per function per entry (211-221), surface_writes checks writes.contains per reference and starts a fresh receiver visited set per reference (589-594), and discovery re-runs every tsc round (main.rs:201).
gaps.counterexample: n entrypoints each export * from './barrel' over n modules: Theta(n^2); n unresolved exported assignments export const f_i = (globalThis as any).g_i.

gaps.summary: Resolution steps scan the whole project on a cache miss: global_symbol_of iterates every file per (file, name) and owner (declarations.rs:1100-1142), superlinear across many files and names; patched_of is one cached O(|G|) pass (2391-2523) charged to whichever node asks first; star export and surface reference tables walk all importers. Build per-file or per-binding indexes at project load with counted work per node.

Project references multiply delegated work: programsOf creates one Program per configuration with no shared document registry, re-parsing files shared through include, and answersOf filters all P programs per query and answers in every applicable one (tsc_sidecar.mjs:301-311).
gaps.counterexample: n referenced tsconfigs whose include covers one shared.ts of size m, with n query sites in shared.ts: parsing Theta(n*m), answering Theta(n^2).

gaps.summary: TscCounts is a per-run aggregate counting only olint's own span indexing (tsc_sidecar.mjs:117-121), not parsing, binding or checker work; it is never attributed per query or node and is requested only through ask_counted in tests, while production (main.rs:18, 166, 202) uses tsc::ask without counts.

Work counts cover one pass only: reset_between_passes replaces the Scheduler, so scheduler_stats reports the final generation and totals across tsc and regex rounds are unobservable; Effects joins, types.rs target dedup, project and tsconfig loading, public discovery (own counter only), discover's function sort (summaries.rs:4700-4741) and all sidecar parsing and checking are never counted, so the counts cannot verify growth order (§7.5).

olint has no memory accounting, and arenas grow across recording passes: summaries_arena is never cleared (reset_between_passes clears only the key map, summaries.rs:807-819, 4747-4780), latent_readings and latent_storage keyed by SummaryId persist, scheduler.callbacks, callback_values and body_sizes carry into each new Scheduler, and the interned trace arena accumulates traces that change between rounds against its global cap. Memory is Theta(R*|G|) under the rounds family.

Scaling tests cannot detect superlinear growth reliably: doubling ratios up to 9/4 (analysis_scaling.rs:1333, 1398) and 3x (2464-2466, 2600-2608) admit n^1.17 and n^1.58, one bound is 200*length (1303), assert_linear_growth is exact but samples three sizes, the compiler tests count only span indexing on a trivial program (1019-1061), no memory is measured, and there are no rounds, generics, union-width, project-reference, nested-loop-prepass, graph-size or memory families. Tighten to exact counts and add the families.

Constant per-node or per-function caps keep per-node work constant (§7.1), but no scaling family in the evaluation corpus backs the lowerings they cause, as §7.4 requires: flow limit 20,000 per function (project.rs:88-90), 32 specializations per function, escape depth 32, Cost MAX_NODES 4096 / MAX_DEPTH 64 / MAX_TEXT 65536 / MAX_REDUCED_TERMS 64, recurrence members 16 / depth 32 / rounds 4, latent depth 6, construction depth 32, class lineage 256, returned-value depth 8, effect scheduling depth 64, value/size/target/alias/lineage/base-class depths, tsc MAXIMUM_CANDIDATE_SYMBOLS 1024, primitive_values limits and the regex source cap of 4096 bytes. Decide whether each cap stays with a §7.4 scaling family as its evidence or goes.
gaps.decision: Matt, 2026-09-29: Keep each per-node cap only where its scaling family shows growth past it; remove the rest.

gaps.summary: More than 1024 tsconfig configurations aborts the whole run (tsconfig.rs:101-106; programsOf throws at tsc_sidecar.mjs:44), with no attribution to nodes.
gaps.counterexample: A root tsconfig referencing n leaf projects fails for n > 1023.
gaps.decision: Matt, 2026-09-29: Lift the 1024-configuration limit once project loading and extends handling are linear (G65, G74, G77).

gaps.summary: remove_lower_priority_files uses IndexMap::shift_remove on the wildcard map, which is O(1) within one name-sorted include bucket but shifts Theta(n) entries per removal when separate include patterns put every .d.ts ahead of its .ts; each project also re-walks its include directories with its own visited set, Theta(P*F) across P overlapping references.
gaps.counterexample: include ["src/**/*.d.ts", "src/**/*.ts"] over n pairs f_i.ts + f_i.d.ts: Theta(n^2).

gaps.summary: The flow graph builder is non-contributing: FlowContext::build/Builder, FlowSummary, FlowFailure, SourceFile::flow/flow_with_limit/flow_context and LoopPhases::iterates are called only by src/flow.test.rs and tests/integration/flow.rs, yet every file builds the oxc control-flow graph (with_cfg(true), project.rs:1579) that only the builder reads. Remove the builder, its entry points and tests, with_cfg(true), the oxc_semantic cfg feature and the oxc_cfg dependency; keep FlowIndex (project.rs:1605, backs SourceFile::children_of) and the used flow.rs items (Completion, Resumption, completion_of, control_target_of, loop_phases_of).

SET_LINEAR 'forEach' and MAP_LINEAR 'forEach', and with it the whole of MAP_LINEAR, are shadowed by the MODELS forEach entries (native.rs:497-510) and dead in effect; method_matters still sees forEach through ARRAY_LINEAR. The other shadowed names stay live through method_matters (types.rs:94), String result-kind inference (declared_types.rs:1671-1675) and TypedArray set, and are kept.

label, write_label and prefer_length_label only read or append to Values.labels, whose readers render text (report.rs:59, 82, 362, 364; main.rs:376; unknowns.rs:371); no cost, state or work count reads them. They are non-contributing to analysis results but feed report text, so action 7.1's test-intent guard likely keeps them; a Phase 1 side note is that first-query label order can change snapshot cost text between root sets.

refuted.summary: Slice 2 marked async-assimilation non-compliant; now gap.
refuted.reason: The counterexample is already covered. For a non-intrinsic operand property_values_of on an input receiver is open and proven_kind is Unknown, so assimilated_reading_of adds a Scheduled Target unknown (invocations.rs:2717-2734); p1 `g(p: PromiseLike<number>)` and p2 `g(p: Promise<number>)` both report O(1) [partial] with an unknown call target at the await. The residual omission is a `then` getter on an external value (property_accessors_of closed when the program defines no `then` accessor, invocations.rs:2633), whose node is already Partial through the Target unknown at the same await origin, so no Known bound is violated. The rule remains a gap for certification only (S2-1). Checked with the working-tree debug build (target/debug/olint.exe, copied to .scratch/olint-compliance/refute-2/) over refute-2/p1..p5 with --types syntactic --min 0; the working-tree edits touch asserted/snapshot recording, not these paths.

refuted.summary: Candidate to confirm in the refutation pass: class-construction-lineage stops silently at an unresolved base class, so `class A extends ExternalBase { x = f(); }` is modelled as its field initialisers only. If the walker adds no implicit super-constructor contribution for the unresolved base, the base's work is missing from `new A()`. Fix: mark the lineage open (unknown contribution) whenever an `extends` base does not resolve.
refuted.reason: The unresolved base is covered. construction_part_of adds base_construction_part_of (walker.rs:2349-2400); base_plan_of calls base_construction_of -> construction_of(heritage expression) (value_targets.rs:2397-2460, 2336-2362), where an unresolved base yields no class candidates and no known targets, so `targets.open |= targets.known.is_empty() && implicit.is_empty()` sets open, plan.open is set, and an UnknownReason::Target contribution is retained (walker.rs:2390-2397). Intermediate constructor-less resolved bases are pushed as implicit and walked the same way. construction_lineage_of only decides whether a Construction node exists; it does not drop base work.

refuted.summary: is_modelled treats every Receiver(Array|Set|Map|String|RegExp) native as modelled and Native::Unmodelled as not; at an intrinsic-replaced call with known user targets the intrinsic alternative is priced only when is_modelled, so an Unmodelled intrinsic (e.g. a conditionally replaced global function or a Kind::Other receiver method) contributes nothing unless open_remainder_of already charged it. Verify in the refutation pass; if confirmed, charge an unknown for the Unmodelled alternative.
refuted.reason: The Unmodelled intrinsic alternative is already charged as an unknown. Whenever intrinsic_replaced_of is true at a call with known targets, those targets are open. For member callees, resolved_callee_within (types.rs:258-261) sets targets.open when member_dispatch_of(..).replaced, which is exactly what intrinsic_replaced_of reads (value_targets.rs:2891). For unbound global identifiers the declaration is not closed, so types.rs:210 sets open. open_remainder_of (HEAD walker.rs:2523-2530) then produces an unknown that every known part retains (walker.rs:2544). The is_modelled branch at walker.rs:2555-2565 only adds a sharper reading beside that unknown. The one residual path is construction_dispatch_of overriding the targets (types.rs:263-266), which concerns constructions rather than this call path.

refuted.summary: No test asserts the invalid unknown value error or the absent-default behaviour directly (default is only compared to warn by stdout).
refuted.reason: src/config.test.rs:28-50 (unknown_policy_has_exact_values_and_warn_default) asserts unknown_policy_of(None) == Warn, the three exact values, and rejection of 'WARN', 'true', false, null, [], {} and 1. §4.8 is covered; no gap.

refuted.summary: The eight golden files (model and tags: expected-lint.txt, expected-lint.exit, expected-report.txt, expected-report-min0.txt) are compared by cli.rs fixtures_print_their_golden_output, with no regenerate command: no package.json script, no env-var bless mode, no tool in tests/. Updating a golden is a hand edit, so a corpus change cannot be produced or reviewed as a diff of tool output.
refuted.reason: Facts are right (cli.rs compares goldens; package.json has no bless script), but no spec clause requires a regenerate command: §5.8 governs programs entering or leaving the corpus, not expected outputs, and the goldens are not the harness's regression indicator. A golden change is already reproducible as a diff of tool output by redirecting the built binary's output, which plan actions 4.1 and 5.2 prescribe. Tooling convenience only.

refuted.summary: The review's 'solver leaves some equivalent composite symbolic expressions incomparable' is confirmed: Cost::compare returns Inconclusive on credit exhaustion, an invalid expression, or when within() fails, and monomial()/dominance handle only products, ratios, constant powers and logs of size dimensions (cost.rs:863-898, 949-1040). It is sound and 4.1 says 'olint proves', so not a violation on its face. It lowers entries to Inconclusive (4.6 fails lint under error), and 5.1 rank comparisons rely on the same procedure. Decide: extend to a complete decision procedure for the expression language, or record the limit in the spec.
refuted.reason: cost.rs:863-898 returns Within only on within(), Exceeds only on within(limit,self) && strictly_larger, else Inconclusive, with a fixed credit budget (deterministic, constant per comparison). The entry itself concedes it is sound. §4.1 and §4.3 make an unproven comparison Inconclusive, which is exactly this behaviour, and no clause requires a complete decision procedure; a stronger comparison is an ordinary improvement. Rank comparison for §5.1 lives in the Phase 1 harness diff, not here.
